# Best Dental Implants in Hackensack, NJ


Specialist Implant Care in the Heart of Bergen County

## Experience the Hackensack Center Difference


At Hackensack Center for Dental Implants, replacing and restoring teeth is not one service among many; it is our entire focus. Every consultation, every treatment plan, and every smile is handled under one roof, with advanced 3D technology, an on-site lab, and a team that treats you like a person, not a case. From a single missing tooth to a full-arch rebuild, we make world-class implant care feel calm, clear, and within reach.

Specialist implant care as our sole focus

Focused expertise for predictable, long-lasting implant outcomes.

Complete treatment under one roof

From 3D imaging and planning to placement and restoration, every step happens here.

On-site dental lab for a custom-fit result

Faster adjustments and precisely crafted restorations without outside delays.

A calm, judgment-free patient experience

Clear guidance, compassionate care, and support at every step of treatment.

More Than New Teeth


## More Than New Teeth, a New Way to Live


Dental implants do more than fill a gap. They give you back the everyday moments that missing or failing teeth take away.


### Smile With Confidence


No more hiding your smile out of fear or embarrassment. With brand new teeth that look, feel, and function like natural teeth


### Regain Your Health


Replacing failing or missing teeth restores full function to your smile, so you can eat the foods you love again and chew comfortably.


### Save Time and Money


With modern technology and an on-site dental lab, we complete the entire process under one roof. That means fewer visits, faster turnaround, and cost efficiencies we pass directly on to you.


### Built to Last


Dental implants are designed as a permanent solution, not a temporary patch.

Precision-trained, patient-first.


## Dr. Alan Meskin, DDS


Dr. Meskin is a prosthodontist dedicated to one thing: replacing and restoring teeth so they look, feel, and function like the ones you were born with. He earned his Doctor of Dental Surgery degree and completed his specialty training in prosthodontics at NYU, then refined his implant work as an associate prosthodontist at ClearChoice, one of the largest dental implant networks in the country. Today he leads Hackensack Center for Dental Implants, where every case is planned in 3D, fabricated in an on-site lab, and designed around the patient sitting in front of him. He provides care in English, Spanish, and Russian.

NYU-trained specialist in replacing and restoring teeth.

## Dental Care, Made Comfortable


Specialist implant care, all under one roof. From your first 3D scan to the day your final teeth are placed, every step of your treatment happens in one place, guided by Dr. Alan Meskin and supported by our on-site lab. No referrals across town, no waiting weeks on an outside lab, and no piecing together your care from multiple offices. It is a simpler, calmer, more coordinated way to restore your smile, designed around your comfort at every step.


### Specialist implant options under one roof.


Every implant is planned in 3D and placed with digital guidance, for a more accurate, less invasive procedure and a faster recovery.


### Comfort and Sedation


Sedation options and a calm, judgment-free team mean even anxious patients feel at ease from start to finish.


### Same-Day Results


Thanks to our on-site lab, many patients walk out with a fixed set of teeth the same day, no long waits, no going without.


### All-on-X, "Teeth in a Day"


Missing multiple teeth? We offer long-term solutions with no slippage, no adhesives, and no compromises. Full arch dental implants use a few carefully placed implants to support a complete smile that feels like you.

More on All-on-X


### Single Tooth Implant


For one missing tooth, a single implant and custom crown look, feel, and function just like a natural tooth, with no impact on the healthy teeth around it.

More on Single Tooth Implants


### Multi-Tooth Implant Bridge


Missing several teeth in a row? An implant-supported bridge fills the gap with strong, natural-looking teeth, anchored by implants rather than relying on neighboring teeth.

More on Implant Bridges

## What to Expect


Every part of a visit to Hackensack Center is designed around your comfort, from the space you walk into, to the technology behind your care, to how we handle the cost.

A Space to Feel at Ease

Care That Never Rushes You

Precision You Can See

Designed and Built Under One Roof

Available Financing Options

Walking in should not feel like the dentist you remember. Our Hackensack office was built to feel calm, with a modern, spa-like reception, a TV in every treatment room, and aromatherapy throughout, so the clinical smell that puts most people on edge is not the first thing you notice.

From your first visit to your final smile, you are cared for by one specialist and one dedicated team, never handed off or rushed. Your first appointment is an unhurried, one-on-one consultation where Dr. Meskin listens to your goals, answers every question, and builds a plan around you. Sedation options are always available, and our coordinators stay with you at every step, so nothing about the process feels overwhelming.

Precision starts with the right tools. We use 3D CBCT imaging and digital scanners to plan every case down to the detail, and our on-site dental lab lets us design and craft your teeth in-house rather than shipping your case out. That means less guesswork, fewer visits, and for many patients, a fixed set of teeth the same day as surgery.

Most practices send your case to an outside lab and wait weeks for it to return. Ours is in the same building. Dr. Meskin and the lab technician design and craft your teeth together, refining the fit and finish in person rather than mailing a case back and forth. It means fewer visits, tighter control over the result, and for many patients, a fixed set of teeth the same day as surgery.

We will work with you using whatever financial options are available to you. We will find a way. We try every avenue, and our dedicated team of treatment coordinators is here to walk you through every detail of your treatment and financing options, so cost never stands between you and the smile you need.

Your journey to a confident smile begins here. We make the process seamless, comfortable, and tailored to deliver results you will love.

Share your smile goals and concerns, and Dr. Meskin will help you find the right treatment for you. This is a relaxed, no-pressure conversation about where you are today and where you want to be.

See your future smile before you commit. Using 3D imaging and digital planning, we map out your treatment and show you the result we are working toward.

With your plan set, Dr. Meskin places and restores your implants using guided digital precision, often with a fixed set of temporary teeth the same day.

Once healing is complete, your final zirconia teeth are placed, and you walk out with restored function and a smile that speaks for itself.

Schedule your consultation today and see how different dental care can feel. At Hackensack Center for Dental Implants, your comfort, your confidence, and your smile are always our priority.

At our practice, we see beauty and oral health as inseparable. Our dedication to health, inspired by the art of creating beautiful smiles, is at the heart of our success.

## Frequently Asked Questions


How much do dental implants cost in Hackensack?

Dental implant costs vary depending on your treatment, since a single tooth implant costs significantly less than a full-arch restoration. After your 3D scan, you'll receive a clear written estimate with no surprises, plus financing options that can bring your cost down to a manageable monthly payment.

Does getting dental implants hurt?

Local anesthesia is used during dental implant placement to manage pain during the procedure. Sedation options may also be available for anxiety. Discomfort, swelling, or soreness afterward varies by patient. Follow your postoperative instructions, and contact the office if pain is severe or worsening.

How long does the process take?

The timeline depends on the number of implants, whether grafting is needed, and how you heal. Some eligible full-arch patients can receive fixed temporary teeth on surgery day, while implant integration may take several months before the final restoration is placed.

I was told I do not have enough bone. Can I still get implants?

Possibly. A 3D CBCT scan can show how much bone is available. Bone grafting or another treatment approach may make implants possible, but only an in-person evaluation can determine whether you are a candidate.

Can a failed or loose implant be fixed?

Often, but the right treatment depends on why the implant is loose or failing and on the surrounding bone and gum tissue. A prosthodontic evaluation and 3D imaging can determine whether the implant can be restored, revised, or needs replacement.

Why see a prosthodontist instead of a general dentist for implants?

Prosthodontists complete three additional years of accredited specialty training after dental school in restoring and replacing teeth. That training is especially relevant to full-arch rehabilitation, complex bite and cosmetic cases, and failed implant restorations.

Do you offer financing and take insurance?

Yes, we offer flexible financing through Cherry, HFD, Proceed, and CareCredit, including low monthly payment options for qualified applicants. While we are not in-network with dental insurance, we verify your benefits and apply them toward your treatment before you begin, so cost never stands between you and the smile you need.

# Privacy policy



# PRIVACY POLICY


Effective Date: September 21, 2026

Aesthetic Dental Center of Hackensack, LLC DBA Hackensack Center for Dental Implants (“Hackensack Center,” “we,” “us,” or “our”) respects your privacy.

This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, disclose, retain, and protect information received through https://www.hackensackdentalimplants.com/ (the “Site”), our text messaging program, and related electronic communications.

This policy applies to prospective patients, current patients, referring professionals, and other individuals who interact with the Site or our communications.

Information maintained in connection with your care may be protected health information (“PHI”) under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (“HIPAA”) and applicable New Jersey law. Our separate Notice of Privacy Practices describes our uses and disclosures of PHI and your rights concerning it.

This Privacy Policy does not replace the Notice of Privacy Practices. If the two conflict concerning PHI, the Notice of Privacy Practices controls.


## 1. INFORMATION WE COLLECT



### Information You Provide


We may collect information you provide when you:

Submit a contact, consultation, appointment-request, referral, or virtual-consultation form.

Schedule or request an appointment.

Opt in to receive text messages.

Communicate with us by telephone, email, text message, or another method.

Provide information in connection with treatment, payment, insurance, or financing.

Submit photographs, imaging, records, or other materials through an authorized method.

Information may include:

Your name, mailing address, email address, and telephone or mobile number.

Appointment preferences, treatment interests, and the reason for contacting us.

Referring-provider information.

Medical and dental history, medications, allergies, imaging, treatment records, and other clinical information.

Insurance, billing, payment, and financing information.

Communications and questions you send to us.

SMS consent status, date and method of consent, opt-out status, and message history.

Other information you voluntarily provide.

Payment-card information may be processed directly by a payment processor and may not be stored by Hackensack Center.


### Information Collected Automatically


When you use the Site, we and our service providers may automatically collect:

IP address and approximate location.

Browser type, operating system, and device information.

Pages viewed, links selected, and time spent on the Site.

Referring website or advertising source.

Cookie identifiers and similar technical information.

Information used to maintain security and diagnose technical problems.

For more information, review our Cookie Policy:

https://www.hackensackdentalimplants.com/cookie-policy


### Health-Related Information


Please do not submit detailed medical histories, clinical records, imaging, diagnoses, financial account details, or similarly sensitive information through a general website form, ordinary email, or SMS.

When sensitive clinical information is necessary, ask our office for an approved secure method.

Health information maintained in connection with your care is handled under HIPAA, applicable New Jersey law, and our Notice of Privacy Practices.


## 2. HOW WE USE INFORMATION


We may use information to:

Respond to questions and requests.

Schedule, confirm, and manage consultations and appointments.

Provide treatment and coordinate care with authorized healthcare professionals.

Send appointment reminders, preparation instructions, and follow-up communications.

Provide two-way customer-care and scheduling communications by text.

Send educational information, practice news, events, and promotional messages when authorized.

Verify insurance benefits, submit claims, and process payments.

Assist with financing applications you initiate.

Operate our on-site laboratory and coordinate the fabrication of dental restorations.

Maintain patient and business records.

Operate, secure, troubleshoot, analyze, and improve the Site.

Measure Site usage and advertising effectiveness.

Prevent fraud, misuse, and security incidents.

Comply with legal, regulatory, professional, and accreditation obligations.

Establish, exercise, or defend legal rights.

We do not use website analytics alone to make clinical decisions concerning your treatment.


## 3. SMS AND TEXT MESSAGING PROGRAM


Hackensack Center offers an SMS/MMS messaging program for appointment communications, conversational support, patient-service messages, educational information, and promotional messages when authorized.


### How You Opt In


You may opt in by:

Entering a mobile number, checking the separate SMS-consent checkbox on a Site form, and submitting the form.

Affirmatively agreeing in writing or electronically to receive text messages.

Using another opt-in method clearly presented by Hackensack Center.

Consent to receive marketing or promotional text messages is not a condition of purchasing products, receiving treatment, or obtaining other services.

By opting in, you consent to receive recurring automated and conversational text messages from Hackensack Center at the number you provide. You represent that you own or are authorized to use that number.

Consent provided to Hackensack Center applies only to communications from Hackensack Center and is not transferable to another business.


### Types of Messages


Messages may include:

Consultation and appointment requests, confirmations, reminders, and rescheduling notices.

Treatment preparation and follow-up communications.

Two-way responses from our staff.

Insurance, financing, billing, and care-coordination messages.

Educational information, service announcements, events, special offers, and practice news when authorized.


### Message Frequency


Message frequency varies depending on your appointments, requests, consent, and interactions with us.


### Message and Data Rates


Message and data rates may apply according to your mobile carrier and plan. Hackensack Center does not charge a separate fee for its messages.


### Opting Out


You may cancel SMS messages at any time by replying STOP. We may send one final message confirming your opt-out. We will then stop sending messages covered by the opt-out unless you subsequently provide new consent.

# All-on-X in Hackensack, NJ


A fixed, full set of teeth for people who are done living with failing teeth or loose dentures. Planned in 3D, placed by a specialist, and in most cases fitted the same day.

JUMP TO SECTION:

Show sections

1. What Is All-on-X?2. What All-on-X Can Fix3. Ideal Candidates4. Why Us?5. All-On-X Process6. Recovery7. Types of Full-Arch Implants8. All-on-X vs a Traditional Denture9. Frequently Asked Questions


## What Is All-on-X?


All-on-X replaces a full arch of teeth, upper, lower, or both, using four to six implants to hold a complete set of fixed teeth in place. The name covers the whole family of full-arch options, so whether your case calls for four implants or six, it falls under the same approach.

What sets it apart from dentures is simple. Nothing comes out. The teeth are anchored to the implants, so they stay put while you eat, talk, and laugh. No adhesives, no slipping, nothing to take out at night.

For most of our patients, the timeline is the part they did not expect. Because we plan everything in 3D beforehand and have our own lab on site, most people leave on the day of surgery with a fixed set of temporary teeth. You are never sent home without a smile.


## What All-on-X Can Fix


Missing and failing teeth change how you eat, speak, and feel around other people. All-on-X is built to address the whole picture, not just the gaps. Here is what it solves most often.

Failing or broken teeth

Loose, slipping dentures

Trouble eating the foods you like

Years of patched-up dental work

Missing most or all of an arch

Ongoing pain or infection


## Who All-on-X Works For


All-on-X is designed for people who have already lost, or are about to lose, most of the teeth in an arch. If you see yourself in any of the reasons below, you are likely a candidate. If you are not sure, come in and Dr. Meskin will give you a straight answer at your consultation.

01

Most of your teeth are failing.

Advanced gum disease, deep decay across several teeth, or old crowns and bridges that keep breaking down all lead to the same place: an arch of teeth where each one has a poor outlook. When your mouth reaches that point, putting more crowns or bridges on teeth that are already failing buys months, not years, and each new failure puts pressure on the teeth next to it. All-on-X clears the arch and rebuilds it as one connected set of teeth in a single planned treatment.

02

Done with your denture.

A full denture rests on your gums and moves around. Over time the jawbone underneath keeps shrinking, the fit gets looser, and the range of foods you can chew narrows. Adhesives are a workaround, not a fix. All-on-X anchors your teeth into your jawbone with four to six implants, so they do not shift, do not need adhesive, and do not come out at night.

03

Years of dental repairs that keep failing.

Root canals redone, crowns remade, bridges replaced, partials adjusted again and again. All of it adds up in cost and time, and the teeth themselves keep getting weaker. Full-arch treatment ends the cycle by replacing the failing teeth with implants that do not decay and do not need root canals. Many of our patients spent years and tens of thousands of dollars on repairs before choosing to fix the whole arch at once.

04

Protecting your face shape.

Your teeth stimulate the bone they sit in. When teeth come out and are not replaced with implants, that bone slowly melts away. The lower part of your face starts to collapse, your chin rotates forward, and your lips lose their support. Traditional dentures actually speed the process up because they press on the gum without giving the bone the pressure it needs to stay strong. Implants give the bone what it needs, and the four-to-six implant pattern used in All-on-X protects the shape of your jaw across the whole arch.

05

Told you cannot have implants.

Not enough bone is the most common reason people are turned away from implants at a general dental office. A specialist looking at the same 3D scan often sees more options:

Placing implants at an angle to make use of the bone you have at the front of your mouth

Adding a small amount of bone only where it is truly needed

Lifting the sinus so implants can go in your upper back jaw

In the most severe upper-jaw cases, longer implants that anchor into your cheekbone


## Why Patients Choose Dr. Meskin for Full-Arch Care


Precision-trained, patient-first.

Dr. Meskin is a prosthodontist dedicated to one thing: replacing and restoring teeth so they look, feel, and function like the ones you were born with. He earned his Doctor of Dental Surgery degree and completed his specialty training in prosthodontics at NYU, then refined his implant work as an associate prosthodontist at ClearChoice, one of the largest dental implant networks in the country. Today he leads Hackensack Center for Dental Implants, where every case is planned in 3D, fabricated in an on-site lab, and designed around the patient sitting in front of him. He provides care in English, Spanish, and Russian.

NYU-trained specialist in replacing and restoring teeth.


## Dr. Alan Meskin, DDS – Credentials

Certificate in Prosthodontics, NYU College of Dentistry

### Dr. Alan Meskin, DDS – Recognition


Patients describe him as an artist with a gentle touch whose restorative work looks so natural no one can tell.

## Your Treatment Journey


All-on-X is a staged surgical and prosthetic case, typically three to six months from the first consultation to the final restoration, with fixed provisional teeth in the mouth for almost the entire interval. The stages below are the same for every case; the specifics change based on your anatomy and the diagnostic findings.


### Consultation and full workup


Your first visit is a real diagnostic appointment. Dr. Meskin examines your remaining teeth and gums, reviews your medical history in detail (some medications and health conditions affect implant healing), and takes a 3D scan of both jaws. The scan is not a formality. It is where your treatment is actually planned. It shows:

Exactly where the nerve runs in your lower jaw, so implants can be placed safely around it

Where your sinuses sit in your upper jaw, so we can plan around them and often avoid needing a sinus lift

How dense your bone is in each spot, which tells us whether your temporary teeth can go in the same day as surgery

The shape of your jawbone, so we can plan a comfortable, natural fit

How the ideal position of your new teeth lines up with the bone we have to anchor them

At the end of the visit, Dr. Meskin walks you through the findings and gives you a written plan. It includes the number of implants, the type of temporary and final teeth, the timeline, and the total cost.


### Designing your new teeth and the surgical guide


Before your surgery is scheduled, your case is designed in detail. Your new teeth are drawn first, shaped around your face, lip line, smile, and bite. Then the implants are positioned virtually against your 3D scan to support those teeth perfectly.

That order matters. Some offices do it in reverse: they place implants wherever the bone is easiest, then try to build teeth to fit. The smile that comes out of that approach is a compromise. Doing it teeth-first is the difference between an average result and one that fits your face.

From that plan, a surgical guide is made. On surgery day, the guide fits over your gum and controls exactly where each implant goes. Placing implants without a guide in a full-arch case invites problems:

Angles that force the teeth into positions you cannot clean easily

Teeth that sit against your gum in ways that trap food and cause irritation

Extra parts and adapters that add cost and weaken the final result

Your fixed temporary teeth are made ahead of time too, ready to attach the same day your implants are placed.


### Surgery day


Surgery happens in one appointment. In that visit:

Any remaining failing teeth in the arch are removed

The gum and bone are prepared using the surgical guide

Four to six implants are placed in the planned positions

Any bone grafting needed at a specific site is done at the same time

Whether your temporary teeth are attached the same day depends on how firmly the implants sit in the bone the moment they go in. When they are solid enough, small connectors are attached, your temporary teeth are secured onto them, and the implants are linked so they share the pressure evenly during healing. If one implant is not quite firm enough for that same-day attachment, we cover it while it heals and you wear a temporary removable set until the final teeth go on. That decision is made during surgery based on what we see, not committed to in advance.

Sedation is available up to IV sedation, so you are comfortable throughout. Most patients tell us the day was much easier than they had feared, and they leave with fixed teeth and clear instructions for the next few days on eating, cleaning, and pain relief.


### Healing


Over the next three to six months, your implants fuse to your jawbone in a process called osseointegration. This is what turns them from placed screws into permanent tooth roots. During this healing time, your temporary teeth are doing more than filling the space. The way they are shaped where they meet your gum guides how your gums heal around each implant, so by the time your final teeth are made, your gum line is already the right shape to frame them.

You wear the temporary teeth normally, eat soft food for the first two weeks, then gradually return to a regular diet, avoiding anything hard or sticky on the temporaries until the finals go on. Check-in visits are short and let Dr. Meskin confirm your implants are integrating well and adjust the temporaries as your gums settle. Most patients are back to their normal day within a week of surgery.


### Your final teeth


Once your implants are fully fused, the temporary teeth come off and your final teeth are made in our on-site lab. Impressions and photos are taken, and the shape, color, length, and how the teeth support your lips are refined right in the chair before your finals are completed.

You have a choice of materials, and Dr. Meskin will walk you through which is better for your situation. Neither is better in every case:

Solid zirconia. The strongest and most stain-resistant option, keeps its polish for years, well-suited to heavy chewers.

Reinforced acrylic teeth on a titanium bar frame. More forgiving under heavy bite pressure, easier to repair in the office, and often the better choice when the teeth in your opposite jaw are still natural.

Your final teeth are attached with tiny screws, not glued in place. That means Dr. Meskin can remove them for deep cleaning and check-ups without damaging anything, and there is no leftover cement below your gum line to cause problems later. Your bite is balanced across the whole arch so the pressure is shared evenly.

## What to Expect From Recovery


Recovery from All-on-X is steadier than most people fear. The first few days bring some swelling and soreness, which most patients manage with over-the-counter care and describe as milder than they expected. The larger part of recovery is quiet: your implants need a few months to fuse with the bone, so you stay on softer foods to protect them while that happens. Follow the aftercare and keep your check-ins, and the process is predictable.


### A Typical All-on-X Recovery Timeline


Every recovery is a little different, but with careful planning and structured aftercare, most patients follow a similar path. Here is a general picture of what healing tends to look like, week by week.


#### Day 0



#### Days 1 to 3


Peak swelling and soreness. Soft foods only. Usually milder than expected.


#### Days 4 to 7


Swelling drops off. Most people return to work.


#### Weeks 2 to 4


Stitches dissolve and gums heal. Still on a soft diet.


#### Months 1 to 3


The bone fuses to your implants. Keep protecting them with softer foods.


#### Months 3 to 6


Final zirconia teeth placed. Back to a normal diet.


## Types of Full-Arch Implants We Offer


Full-arch care is not one-size-fits-all. Depending on your jaw, your bone, and your goals, Dr. Meskin will recommend the option that fits you best. Here are the main approaches.

All-on-4

The classic full-arch solution. Four implants, angled for maximum grip in the available bone, support a complete fixed set of teeth. It often works even when bone is limited, which is why so many patients qualify without extra grafting.

All-on-6

For patients with more bone or who want extra support, six implants spread the load further. It can mean added stability and is often used for the upper jaw, where bone tends to be softer.

Fixed Zirconia Bridge

Your final teeth, made from solid zirconia. It is stronger, more natural-looking, and more stain-resistant than the acrylic most offices use, and it is designed to last for years.

Same-Day Fixed Temporaries

The fixed set you leave with on surgery day. Not a denture you take out, but teeth anchored to your new implants while everything heals, so you are never without a smile.


### Upper Arch All-on-X


Restoring the top arch has its own challenges, softer bone and the sinuses nearby. Our 3D planning maps around both so placement is precise and secure.


### Lower Arch All-on-X


The lower jaw is usually denser, which often makes it an ideal candidate for a fixed full arch, sometimes with a very smooth path to same-day teeth.


### Snap-In Overdenture


The removable alternative. It clips onto implants for far more hold than a traditional denture, but comes out for cleaning. A good fit for some, though most of our patients prefer a fixed set.


### Full-Mouth (Both Arches)


For patients who need both the upper and lower restored, we rebuild the entire smile together, planned as one so the bite, look, and function all line up.

Book A Consultation


## All-on-X vs a Traditional Denture


A removable denture is the most economical way to replace a full arch, but it comes with real trade-offs for your health, comfort, and appearance. Here is how fixed All-on-X teeth compare, point by point.

All-on-X (Fixed Teeth)

Removable Denture

Retention

Anchored to implants in the jaw, so they never slip or move.

Rests on the gums and can slip or shift, especially when eating or speaking.

Stability

Stable enough to bite and chew almost like natural teeth.

Less stable, so chewing and speaking can be difficult.

Comfort

No pressure on the gums, no sore spots, no adhesive.

Can rub and irritate the gums, and often needs adhesive to stay put.

Jawbone Health

Implants act like tooth roots and preserve the jawbone and facial support.

Bone keeps shrinking underneath, which changes your bite and ages the face over time.

Appearance

Designed around your face for a natural look.

Can look bulky or artificial and may shift when you smile or talk.

Durability

Built to last for years, often for life with proper care.

Wears out and needs relines or remakes every few years.

Cost

Higher upfront, but better value over the long run.

Lower upfront, though repeat repairs and remakes add up.

## Frequently Asked Questions


How much does All-on-X cost in Hackensack?

It depends on your case, whether it is one arch or both, and what needs to happen before the implants go in. After your 3D scan you get a clear written estimate with no surprises, plus financing that can bring it down to a monthly payment.

Does All-on-X hurt?

Most patients are surprised by how comfortable it is. The procedure is done with sedation, and the soreness afterward is usually managed with simple over-the-counter care.

Will I really leave with teeth the same day?

In most cases, yes. You go home with a fixed set of temporary teeth on the day of surgery, then receive your final zirconia set once you have healed.

I was told I do not have enough bone. Can I still get All-on-X?

Often yes. All-on-4 is designed to work with limited bone, and modern 3D planning solves cases that would have been turned away years ago. A scan is the only way to know for sure.

How long until I can eat normally?

You are on softer foods while your implants fuse, usually a few months. Once your final teeth are placed, you can get back to a normal diet.

Why see a prosthodontist for All-on-X?

A prosthodontist trains for years specifically in replacing and restoring teeth. For full-arch work, where both function and appearance matter, that specialization means a more predictable, natural-looking result.

Do you offer financing?

Yes. We work with Cherry, HFD, Proceed, and CareCredit, and our treatment coordinators will help you find a plan that fits. We also verify any insurance benefits up front.

# Single Tooth Implants in Hackensack, NJ


The most natural, permanent way to replace one missing or failing tooth, without touching the healthy teeth beside it. Designed and placed by a prosthodontist so it blends right in.

JUMP TO SECTION:

Show sections

1. What Is a Single Tooth Implant?2. What a Single Tooth Implant Can Fix3. Candidate4. Why Us5. Process6. Recovery7. Single Tooth Implant vs a Dental Bridge8. Finance9. Frequently Asked Questions


## What Is a Single Tooth Implant?


A single tooth implant replaces one missing tooth from the root up. A small titanium post takes the place of the root, a connector called an abutment sits on top, and a custom crown finishes it off. Together they look, feel, and work like a natural tooth.

What makes it different from a bridge is important. An implant stands on its own. It does not lean on the teeth next to it, which means those healthy teeth are left completely alone. A bridge, by contrast, only works by grinding down the two teeth on either side of the gap to anchor it.

Because the post sits in the bone the way a real root did, it also keeps the jawbone stimulated and healthy. You care for it exactly like a natural tooth. Brush it, floss it, and it can last for many years.


## What a Single Tooth Implant Can Fix


Losing or damaging a single tooth affects more than one spot in your mouth. Left alone, the gap changes your bite and the bone beneath it. A single implant solves the whole problem at the source.

A tooth lost to decay

A tooth knocked out by injury

A cracked tooth beyond saving

A failed root canal

A tooth too broken to hold a filling or crown

A missing tooth causing others to shift


## Who is a Good Candidate for a Single Tooth Implant?


Most adults missing a tooth, or about to lose one, are candidates for a single implant. A few things need to be in place for treatment to succeed, and we check all of them at your consultation.

01

Healthy neighboring teeth and enough room in the gap

This is the part that is unique to replacing a single tooth. The implant has to sit in the gap without crowding the teeth on either side, and those neighbors need to be healthy in their own right.

Enough space in the gap, generally a few millimeters of clearance from each neighboring tooth

Neighboring teeth that are healthy and stable on their own roots

If teeth have drifted or tipped into the gap over time, the space may need to be reopened first

02

Enough healthy bone at the site

The implant fuses directly to the jawbone, so there has to be enough bone in that specific spot to hold it securely. Bone naturally begins to shrink the moment a tooth is lost, and the longer the gap has been there, the more it recedes. Your cone beam scan measures the height and width of bone available, and if there is not quite enough, a small, focused graft can rebuild the site before or at the time of placement. This is very routine for a single implant and adds only a little to the overall timeline.

03

Healthy gums

Because the implant emerges through the gum, the gum tissue around it needs to be free of active infection. Gum disease is one of the most common reasons a tooth is lost in the first place, and if it is still present it can spread to the tissue around a new implant and stop it from fusing. If we find any active gum disease, we treat and control it first, which protects both the implant and the rest of your teeth.

04

A stable, balanced bite

A single crown has to fit into your existing bite so that it takes a fair share of the load and no more. If your bite is uneven, or if you clench or grind your teeth at night, an implant crown can be placed under more force than it should carry. We check for this during planning and, where needed, adjust the crown or provide a nightguard so your new tooth is protected for the long term.

05

Good general health, ideally a non-smoker

As with any minor surgery, your body needs to be able to heal well. Most healthy adults qualify, and well-controlled conditions such as managed diabetes are usually fine, though anything that affects healing is something we plan around. Smoking is the one habit we ask you to pause, because it slows healing and meaningfully raises the risk of implant failure, both while the implant fuses and for years afterward.


## Why Patients Choose Dr. Meskin to Replace a Tooth


Precision-trained, patient-first.

Dr. Meskin is a prosthodontist dedicated to one thing: replacing and restoring teeth so they look, feel, and function like the ones you were born with. He earned his Doctor of Dental Surgery degree and completed his specialty training in prosthodontics at NYU, then refined his implant work as an associate prosthodontist at ClearChoice, one of the largest dental implant networks in the country. Today he leads Hackensack Center for Dental Implants, where every case is planned in 3D, fabricated in an on-site lab, and designed around the patient sitting in front of him. He provides care in English, Spanish, and Russian.

## Your Treatment Journey


A single tooth implant is carried out in clear stages, so you always know what comes next. From first consultation to final crown, most cases take a few months, with most of that time spent letting the implant heal.


### Consultation and 3D Planning


Your first visit is about understanding your mouth and confirming an implant is the right move before anything else happens. Dr. Meskin reviews your history, examines the gap and the teeth around it, and takes a 3D cone beam scan so the whole case is planned against your exact anatomy. Because this visit covers a lot, here is what it includes:

Assessing the gap, your bite, and the health of the neighboring teeth

A 3D scan that measures the bone and locates the nerves and sinuses to avoid

Flagging anything needed first, such as removing a failing tooth or a small graft

A firm written estimate, a timeline, and a conversation about sedation if you want it


### Removing the Tooth and Preparing the Site


This step only applies if the tooth is still in place or the site needs building up. If a failing tooth has to come out, we remove it as gently as possible and, in many cases, place a small bone graft into the socket at the same time to preserve the bone for the implant. Where a tooth has been missing for a while and the bone has already shrunk, a graft rebuilds the site first. If your bone is already healthy and the gap is ready, we skip straight to placement.


### Placing the Implant


Placement is a focused, minor procedure, often done in under an hour and comfortable enough that most people are surprised afterward. We make sure you are numb and relaxed, with sedation if you chose it, then set the titanium post into the jawbone in the exact position from your plan through a small opening in the gum. A healing cap is usually added on top to shape the gum for a natural crown margin. If the gap shows when you smile, we fit a temporary tooth so you never leave with a visible space.


### Healing and Osseointegration


This is the quiet stretch that does most of the work. Over the next few months the implant fuses with your jawbone, a process called osseointegration, which is what gives the finished tooth its strength and permanence. There is little to notice day to day. You stay on normal foods, chewing on the other side near the site, and we see you for a quick check or two to confirm healing is on track.


### Fitting Your Final Crown


Once the implant has fully fused, you come back for the part that makes it look like it was always there. We take a detailed impression and craft a crown matched to the shade and shape of the teeth beside it, then secure it to the implant, usually with a small screw through the top that we cover with tooth-colored filling so it is invisible. The finished tooth looks, feels, and works like the one you lost, and Dr. Meskin continues to care for it long term.


## Watch Our Patient Video Diaries


Hear from patients who replaced a tooth and stopped thinking about it, in their own words.

View All Testimonials


## What to Expect From Recovery


Recovery from a single implant is usually mild. Most people have a little soreness or swelling for a day or two, easily managed with over-the-counter care, and are back to their normal routine quickly. The longer part is quiet and hands-off: the post needs a few months to fuse with the bone before the final crown goes on. During that time you simply protect the area and eat a little more carefully.


### A Typical Single Implant Timeline


Every case is a little different, but most single implants follow a similar path from placement to final crown. Here is a general picture of what to expect.


#### Day 0


Implant placed. Mild soreness or swelling is normal.


#### Days 1 to 3


Most people return to work and normal activity.


#### Days 4 to 7


Any soreness settles. Eat carefully around the site.


#### Weeks 2 to 4


Gum tissue heals over the implant.


#### Months 1 to 3


The post fuses with the bone.


#### Months 3 to 6


Abutment and custom crown placed. Your tooth is complete.


## Single Tooth Implant vs a Dental Bridge


For years, a bridge was the standard way to replace one missing tooth. An implant does the same job without the biggest drawback of a bridge, which is grinding down the healthy teeth on either side. Here is how the two compare, point by point.

Single Tooth Implant

Dental Bridge

Healthy teeth

Stands on its own. The teeth on either side are never touched.

The two neighboring teeth must be ground down to hold the bridge, even if they are healthy.

Jawbone health

The post acts like a tooth root and preserves the bone where the tooth was lost.

Does nothing for the bone under the gap, which continues to shrink over time.

Stability and function

Fixed in the jaw, with biting strength close to a natural tooth.

Solid, but relies on the strength of the teeth it is cemented to.

Appearance

The crown emerges from the gum like a real tooth, matched to blend in.

Looks good, but the false tooth rests on the gum rather than growing from it.

Cleaning

Brush and floss like a normal tooth.

You have to clean underneath the false tooth with special floss or picks.

Longevity

Designed to last for many years, often for life with good care.

Typically needs replacing every 10 to 15 years, and the ground-down teeth stay altered for good.

Cost

Higher upfront, better value over the long run.

Lower upfront, but repeat replacements and risk to the anchor teeth add up.

Schedule your consultation today and see how natural replacing one tooth can look. At Hackensack Center for Dental Implants, your comfort, your confidence, and your smile always come first.


## Frequently Asked Questions


How much does a single tooth implant cost in Hackensack?

It depends on your case, including whether the old tooth needs removing or the site needs a graft. After your 3D scan you receive a clear written estimate with no surprises, plus financing that can bring it down to a monthly payment.

Is an implant better than a bridge?

For most people, yes, because an implant leaves the neighboring teeth untouched and keeps the jawbone healthy, while a bridge grinds down two healthy teeth to anchor it. A bridge can still make sense if those neighboring teeth already need crowns, and Dr. Meskin will tell you honestly which fits your situation.

Does getting a single implant hurt?

Most patients find it more comfortable than they expected, often easier than the extraction that sometimes comes first. It is done with local anesthetic, sedation is available, and any soreness afterward is usually mild.

How long does the whole process take?

Usually a few months from start to finish. The post placement is quick, but the implant needs three to six months to fuse with the bone before the final crown is placed.

Can I get the implant and tooth the same day?

Sometimes. In certain cases the implant can be placed the day the old tooth is removed, and a temporary can be fitted. Whether that is right for you depends on the bone and the site, which the scan will show.

Will the crown match my other teeth?

That is the whole point of seeing a prosthodontist. Your crown is designed in our lab to match the shade and shape of the teeth around it, so it blends in rather than stands out.

Do you offer financing?

Yes. We work with Cherry, HFD, Proceed, and CareCredit, and our treatment coordinators will help you find a plan that fits. We also verify any insurance benefits up front.

# Implant Revision in Hackensack, NJ


A failing, loose, or painful implant does not always mean starting over. If an implant placed elsewhere has let you down, Dr. Meskin can often diagnose it, save what can be saved, and rebuild what cannot.

JUMP TO SECTION:

## What Is Implant Revision and Why Expertise Matters


Implant revision is the diagnosis and repair of an implant that is failing, loose, painful, or simply was not done right the first time. Sometimes that means treating an infection and saving the implant. Sometimes it means removing it, letting the site heal, and placing a new one. And sometimes it means redoing a crown, bridge, or full arch that never fit or looked the way it should.

Revision is harder than the original procedure, not easier. The specialist has to work out why the first attempt failed, deal with any bone or gum damage left behind, and then rebuild in a way that lasts. That takes a level of training most general dentists do not have.

This is exactly the kind of case a prosthodontist is built for. Dr. Meskin spends his days on complex implant and full-mouth work, including the cases other offices would rather refer out than take on.

A second opinion costs you nothing but an hour, and it frequently changes the picture entirely. Many implants written off elsewhere turn out to be treatable once someone looks closely with the right tools.

Your implant is loose, painful, or feels wrong

An infection or gum problem has developed around it

The crown or bridge never fit or matched your other teeth

A full-arch case does not look or function the way you were promised

The implant failed completely and you were told it could not be redone

You simply want an honest, specialist opinion before doing anything more


## Why Patients Seek a Second Opinion


Most people who come to us for revision are not first-time patients. They have already been through an implant somewhere else, and something is wrong. Maybe it hurts. Maybe it moves. Maybe the crown never matched, or the whole thing simply failed. Often they were told nothing more could be done, or were left unsure who to trust next.


## What Implant Revision Can Fix


A problem implant affects more than one tooth. It can hurt, harbor infection, damage the bone around it, and leave you afraid to chew on that side. Revision addresses the whole situation, not just the visible part. Here are the problems it solves most often.

01

A Loose or Painful Implant

Movement or ongoing pain means something is wrong beneath the surface. Revision finds the cause and either stabilizes the implant or replaces it.

02

Infection Around an Implant

Peri-implantitis, the infection that attacks the gum and bone around an implant, is treated directly, protecting the bone before more is lost.

03

A Failed Implant

When an implant has failed completely, the site is cleaned, rebuilt if needed, and a new implant is placed on a solid foundation.

04

A Poor Crown, Bridge, or Arch

When the restoration on top never fit, matched, or functioned properly, Dr. Meskin redesigns and remakes it in our lab so it finally looks and works right.


## Why Patients Come to Dr. Meskin for a Revision


Precision-trained, patient-first.

Dr. Meskin is a prosthodontist dedicated to one thing: replacing and restoring teeth so they look, feel, and function like the ones you were born with. He earned his Doctor of Dental Surgery degree and completed his specialty training in prosthodontics at NYU, then refined his implant work as an associate prosthodontist at ClearChoice, one of the largest dental implant networks in the country. Today he leads Hackensack Center for Dental Implants, where every case is planned in 3D, fabricated in an on-site lab, and designed around the patient sitting in front of him. He provides care in English, Spanish, and Russian.

## How Dr. Meskin Approaches a Revision


Every revision follows the same first step, a proper diagnosis, and then splits into different paths depending on what we find. Some cases stay non-surgical. Some involve removal, healing, and replacement. Dr. Meskin will tell you which one applies to you after the workup, with a clear plan and a firm estimate before you commit to anything.


### Diagnostic Workup


Your first visit is where the real work happens. We review your history, examine the existing implant, and take a 3D cone beam scan to see what is going on around and beneath the site. This visit covers a lot:

Clinical exam of the implant, gum, and surrounding teeth

Full mouth photographs and diagnostic impressions

3D scan to measure bone loss, evaluate the implant position, and check for infection

Review of your bite and how it loads onto the implant

Review of any existing records or x-rays from the original placement

A written diagnosis and plan, with a firm estimate, before anything else happens


### Save or Replace Decision


Based on the workup, we tell you what the options are. Broadly, cases go one of three ways.

Non-surgical revision. The implant is sound. The problem is on top of it or in the bite. Fixed by redesigning the restoration, adjusting the bite, or treating a soft-tissue issue.

Save the implant surgically. The implant is still integrated but has infection or early bone loss around it. Treated with deep cleaning, sometimes surgery to clean the implant surface, and often a new restoration.

Remove and rebuild. The implant cannot be saved. It is removed, the site is treated, and a new implant is planned when the site is ready.


### Treatment


The treatment stage depends on the path. Non-surgical revisions may be complete in one to two visits. Surgical save cases involve a small procedure and a healing period. Remove-and-rebuild cases involve removal, sometimes bone grafting, and eventually a new implant. All of it is done under local anesthetic, with sedation available if you want it.


### Healing and Osseointegration


If a new implant is placed, the healing period is where bone fuses with it. That takes a few months, and revision sites sometimes take a little longer than a first-time site because the surrounding bone has already been through one procedure. We see you back for a check or two to confirm healing is on track. Studies report second implants in previously failed sites succeed at around 88 to 93 percent when the underlying cause is diagnosed and corrected first.


### Final Restoration and Follow-Up


The final crown, bridge, or full-arch is made in the on-site lab, matched to the shade and shape of the teeth around it, and adjusted so the bite loads evenly across the site. From there, we see you back for check-ins to make sure the result stays healthy. Regular cleanings and follow-up are especially important for revision patients, because the goal is to make sure the cause that failed the first implant does not repeat.

## Frequently Asked Questions


Can a failed or loose implant really be fixed?

Often, yes. Some struggling implants are saved by treating the infection or replacing a component. Others need to be removed, with a new implant placed after the site heals. The only way to know which applies to you is a 3D scan and an exam.

I was told my implant could not be saved. Is that true?

Maybe, but it is worth a second opinion. Even implants that have failed completely can usually be redone after the site heals, sometimes with a bone graft. Being told no at one office does not always mean no everywhere.

Why did my implant fail?

The common causes are infection around the implant, an implant that never fully fused with the bone, bone loss, too much bite pressure from grinding, or a placement that was not quite right. Part of revision is working out exactly which it was, so it does not happen again.

Does implant revision hurt?

It is done with local anesthetic and sedation is available. Many revision steps, like treating an infection or replacing a component, are minor. Dr. Meskin will walk you through what your specific case involves.

How much does implant revision cost?

It depends entirely on what needs to be done, from a simple component replacement to a full removal, graft, and new implant. After your scan you receive a clear written estimate, plus financing options.

Will I be without a tooth during the process?

Usually not for long. Where a temporary is possible, one is provided so you are not left with a visible gap while the site heals.

Do you offer financing?

Yes. We work with Cherry, HFD, Proceed, and CareCredit, and our treatment coordinators will help you find a plan that fits. We also verify any insurance benefits up front.

# Implant Bridges in Hackensack, NJ


Missing several teeth in a row? An implant-supported bridge replaces them with fixed, natural-looking teeth, using just a couple of implants and without grinding down the healthy teeth beside the gap.

JUMP TO SECTION:

Show sections

1. What Is an Implant Bridge?2. The Benefits of an Implant Bridge3. Candidate4. Why Us5. Process6. Recovery7. Types of Implant Bridges8. Implant Bridge vs a Traditional Bridge9. Financing10. Frequently Asked Questions


## What Is an Implant Bridge?


An implant bridge replaces two or more missing teeth in a row using implants instead of grinding down the healthy teeth next to the gap. In most cases, two implants anchor a bridge of three or four teeth, so the whole span is held firmly in the jaw rather than resting on the neighbors.

Each implant is a small titanium post that fuses with your jawbone and takes the place of a tooth root. On top of them sits a single fixed bridge, custom-made to look and function like your natural teeth. Nothing clips in and nothing rests on your gums.

An implant bridge sits between two other options. It is more efficient than placing one implant per missing tooth, and healthier than a traditional bridge that has to lean on the neighboring teeth. For patients missing several teeth in a row, it is usually the best balance of the two.


## The Benefits of an Implant Bridge


Replacing missing teeth with an implant bridge is not only about closing the gap. It restores what a bridge sitting on the gum or a traditional bridge on the neighbors cannot.

Healthy teeth left untouched

Preserves your jawbone

Bite strength close to natural teeth

Fixed, never removed

Natural, seamless look

Long-lasting, often for life


## Who Is a Good Candidate for an Implant Bridge?


Most adults missing two or more teeth in a row are good candidates for an implant bridge. A few things specific to a multi-tooth span matter, and we check all of them at your consultation. A 3D scan gives us a definite answer.

01

Two or more missing teeth in a row

An implant bridge is designed for a span, not a single gap. It works best when you are missing two, three, or four teeth in a row, held by two implants at either end of the span. Longer spans, or gaps at the very back of the mouth, may need a third implant for extra support. If you are missing just one tooth, a single implant is usually the better call, and we will tell you honestly which fits your situation.

02

Enough healthy bone at both implant sites

Because a bridge is anchored at both ends, there has to be enough bone in both spots to hold each implant securely. This is often where a multi-tooth case gets more interesting than a single one, since the gap has usually been there long enough for the bone to start shrinking.

Your 3D scan measures bone height and width at each planned implant site

If bone is thin in one or both spots, a small graft can rebuild it before or during placement

Angled placement can sometimes work around limited bone without a graft

We plan around the nerves and sinuses so placement stays safe and precise

03

Healthy gums

Because the implants and the bridge margin all sit against the gum, the tissue around them needs to be free of active infection. Gum disease is one of the most common reasons multi-tooth loss happens in the first place, and if it is still active, it can spread to the tissue around the new implants and stop them from fusing. Any active gum disease is treated and controlled first, which protects both the bridge and the rest of your teeth.

04

A stable, balanced bite

A bridge that spans several teeth takes a real share of the load when you chew. If your bite is uneven, or if you clench or grind at night, that load can concentrate on the wrong point and stress the bridge over time. During planning, Dr. Meskin studies how your teeth come together and, where needed, adjusts the bridge or provides a nightguard so it is protected for the long term.

05

Good general health, ideally a non-smoker

Most healthy adults qualify. Well-controlled conditions such as managed diabetes are usually fine, and anything that affects healing is something we plan around. Smoking is the one habit we ask you to pause, because it slows healing and meaningfully raises the risk of implant failure, both while the implants fuse and for years afterward.


## Why Patients Choose Dr. Meskin for an Implant Bridge


Precision-trained, patient-first.

Dr. Meskin is a prosthodontist dedicated to one thing: replacing and restoring teeth so they look, feel, and function like the ones you were born with. He earned his Doctor of Dental Surgery degree and completed his specialty training in prosthodontics at NYU, then refined his implant work as an associate prosthodontist at ClearChoice, one of the largest dental implant networks in the country. Today he leads Hackensack Center for Dental Implants, where every case is planned in 3D, fabricated in an on-site lab, and designed around the patient sitting in front of him. He provides care in English, Spanish, and Russian.


## Dr. Alan Meskin, DDS – Credentials


NYU-trained specialist in replacing and restoring teeth.

Doctor of Dental Surgery (DDS), NYU College of Dentistry

Certificate in Prosthodontics, NYU College of Dentistry

Associate Prosthodontist, ClearChoice Dental Implant Centers


### Dr. Alan Meskin, DDS – Recognition


The work speaks through the patients who wear it.

Patients describe him as an artist with a gentle touch whose restorative work looks so natural no one can tell.

4.7 stars on Google with over 1,000 reviews.

Complex and referred-out cases trusted to him by other dental offices.

## Your Treatment Journey


An implant bridge is completed in clear stages, from consultation to final placement. Most cases take a few months, mainly to allow the implants to heal. We’ll guide you through the steps your treatment requires.


### Consultation and 3D Planning


Your first visit is about understanding your mouth and confirming an implant bridge is the right move before anything else happens. Dr. Meskin reviews your history, examines the span and the teeth around it, and takes a 3D cone beam scan so the whole case is planned against your exact anatomy. Because this visit covers a lot, here is what it includes:

Assessing the span, your bite, and the health of the neighboring teeth

A 3D scan that measures the bone at each planned implant site

Deciding how many implants your span needs, usually two, sometimes three

Flagging anything needed first, such as removing failing teeth or a small graft

A firm written estimate, a timeline, and a conversation about sedation if you want it


### Removing Failing Teeth and Preparing the Sites


This step only applies if there are still teeth in the span that need to come out, or if the bone at the implant sites needs building up. Where the bone is already healthy and the span is ready, we skip straight to placement.

Failing teeth are removed as gently as possible under local anesthetic

A small graft often goes into the socket at the same time to preserve bone

If the gap has been there a while, a focused graft rebuilds the site first

Healing between this step and placement varies from immediate to a few months


### Placing the Implants


Placement is a precise, guided procedure. Most patients find it easier than they expected, and we make sure you are numb and relaxed before we begin, with sedation if you chose it. Two implants are set into the jawbone at the ends of the span, in the exact positions from your plan, so the load of the future bridge is carried by strong anchor points at each end.

Healing caps are usually fitted on top to shape the gum for a natural bridge margin. If the span shows when you smile, we provide a temporary bridge on the same day so you never leave with a visible gap.


### Healing and Osseointegration


This is the quiet stretch that does most of the work. Over the next few months, the implants fuse with the jawbone, a process called osseointegration, which is what gives the finished bridge its strength and permanence. There is little to notice day to day. You stay on softer foods early on and gradually return to a normal diet, and we see you for a check or two to confirm healing is on track.


### Fitting Your Final Crown


Once the implants are fully fused, you come back for the part that makes it look like it was always there. This is where the prosthodontic side of the work actually pays off, since the bridge has to blend into the teeth around it and share the bite evenly across two anchor points.

A detailed impression is taken of both implants and the surrounding teeth

Your bridge is crafted to match the shade, shape, and gum line of your other teeth

It is secured to the implants, usually with hidden screws under tooth-colored filling

Dr. Meskin fine-tunes the bite so the load is shared evenly across the span

We continue to care for the result long term with regular check-ins


## Watch Our Patient Video Diaries


Hear from patients who rebuilt a whole section of their smile, in their own words.

View All Testimonials


## What to Expect From Recovery


Recovery from an implant bridge is usually straightforward. Most people have some soreness or swelling for a couple of days, easily managed with over-the-counter care, and get back to their routine quickly. The longer part is quiet: the implants need a few months to fuse with the bone before the final bridge goes on. During that stretch you protect the area and stick to softer foods, often with a temporary in place so you are never left with a visible gap.


### A Typical Implant Bridge Timeline


Every case is a little different, but most implant bridges follow a similar path from placement to final bridge. Here is a general picture of what to expect.


#### Day 0


Implants placed, temporary fitted if needed. Some swelling is normal.


#### Days 1 to 3


Most people return to work and normal activity.


#### Days 4 to 7


Any soreness settles. Eat carefully around the site.


#### Weeks 2 to 4


Gum tissue heals over the implants.


#### Months 1 to 3


The implants fuse with the bone.


#### Months 3 to 6


Abutments and custom bridge placed. Your smile is complete.


## Types of Implant Bridges


The number of implants depends on how many teeth are missing and where the gap sits in your mouth. Dr. Meskin recommends the option that gives you the strongest, longest-lasting result for your case.

Three-Unit Implant Bridge

The most common type. Two implants anchor a bridge of three teeth, with a false tooth in the middle. It is a strong, predictable solution for the most common gap, three missing teeth in a row.

Four-Unit Implant Bridge

Two implants can also support a slightly longer bridge of four teeth, with two false teeth in the middle. It is more efficient than placing an implant for every tooth and still gives you a solid, non-removable result.

Longer-Span Bridge

For longer gaps or spans that need extra support, a third implant is added in the middle. This spreads the load and is often used at the back of the mouth, where biting forces are highest.

Cantilever Implant Bridge

In select cases, a bridge can extend a false tooth beyond the last implant, useful when a gap sits at the very back of the mouth and a second implant is not possible. It is used carefully and only where the bite and bone allow it.


### Front-of-Mouth Implant Bridge


Bridges in the front of the mouth face different challenges: less biting force, but every millimeter of shade, shape, and gum line has to look right. As a prosthodontist, matching a front bridge to your face is Dr. Meskin's specialty.


### Back-of-Mouth Implant Bridge


Molars carry the most biting force in your mouth, so bridges here are built for strength. Implant placement and bridge material are chosen to hold up under years of real chewing.

Book A Consultation


## Implant Bridge vs a Traditional Bridge


For years, a traditional tooth-supported bridge was the standard way to replace several teeth in a row. An implant bridge does the same job without the biggest drawback of a traditional bridge, which is grinding down the healthy teeth on either side of the gap. Here is how the two compare, point by point.

Implant Bridge

Traditional Bridge

Healthy teeth

Stands on its own implants. The teeth next to the gap are never touched.

The two neighboring teeth must be ground down to hold the bridge, even when healthy.

Jawbone health

The implants act like tooth roots and preserve the bone across the span.

Does nothing for the bone under the gap, which continues to shrink over time.

Stability and bite

Fixed in the jaw, with biting strength close to natural teeth.

Solid, but its strength depends on the two anchor teeth holding it up.

Appearance

Emerges from the gum like natural teeth, matched to blend in.

Looks good, but the false teeth rest on the gum rather than growing from it.

Cleaning

Cleaned with normal brushing and a special floss under the bridge.

Requires floss threaders or picks to clean under the false teeth every day.

Longevity

Designed to last many years, often for life with proper care.

Typically needs replacing every 10 to 15 years, and the ground-down teeth stay altered for good.

Cost

Higher upfront, better value over the long run.

Lower upfront, but repeat replacements and risk to the anchor teeth add up.

Schedule your consultation today and see how naturally a whole section of your smile can be rebuilt. At Hackensack Center for Dental Implants, your comfort, your confidence, and your smile always come first.


## Frequently Asked Questions


How much does an implant bridge cost in Hackensack?

It depends on how many teeth you are replacing, how many implants your case needs, and whether any grafting or extractions are involved. After your 3D scan you receive a clear written estimate with no surprises, plus financing that can bring it down to a monthly payment.

How many implants do I need for a bridge?

Usually two, one at each end of the gap, to support a bridge of three or four teeth. Longer spans can call for a third implant. Your scan tells us exactly what your case needs.

Is an implant bridge better than a traditional bridge?

For most people, yes. An implant bridge does not grind down the healthy teeth beside the gap, and it preserves the jawbone the way a traditional bridge cannot. A traditional bridge can still make sense if those neighboring teeth already need crowns, and Dr. Meskin will tell you honestly which fits your case.

Does getting an implant bridge hurt?

Most patients find it more comfortable than expected. The implants are placed under local anesthetic, sedation is available, and any soreness afterward is usually mild.

How long does the process take?

Usually a few months from start to finish. Placing the implants is quick, but they need three to six months to fuse with the bone before the final bridge is fitted.

Will I have a gap while it heals?

Usually not. In most cases a temporary can be worn during the healing months, so you are not left with a visible space.

Do you offer financing?

Yes. We work with Cherry, HFD, Proceed, and CareCredit, and our treatment coordinators will help you find a plan that fits. We also verify any insurance benefits up front.

# Full-Mouth Rehabilitation in Hackensack, NJ


For a mouth that needs more than one repair. Dr. Meskin rebuilds worn, broken, and failing teeth into a healthy, comfortable, natural-looking smile, planned as one whole rather than a series of patches.

JUMP TO SECTION:

Show sections

1. What Is Full-Mouth Rehabilitation?2. Understanding Full-Mouth Rehabilitation3. Why Us?4. What Your Rehabilitation Can Include5. Your Treatment Journey6. The Rehabilitation Timeline7. Frequently Asked Questions


## What Is Full-Mouth Rehabilitation?


Full-mouth rehabilitation is a coordinated plan to rebuild the health, function, and appearance of most or all of your teeth in both jaws. It is not a single procedure. It is a full strategy that combines whichever treatments you actually need, whether implants, crowns, veneers, bridges, gum treatment, or bite correction, and sequences them in a logical order over months, not years.

The point of doing it as one plan, rather than treatment by treatment, is that the pieces have to fit together. Your bite, your gums, the bone underneath, and the way the teeth meet all affect each other. Handling them separately, spread across different offices, is how patients end up with work that fails a few years later.

At Hackensack Center, your case is planned and delivered by Dr. Meskin, an NYU-trained prosthodontist whose specialty is exactly this: rebuilding a whole mouth so the result is stable, comfortable, and looks like teeth that belong to your face.


## Understanding Full-Mouth Rehabilitation


When Full-Mouth Rehab Is the Right Move

Full-mouth rehab is for people whose problems have stacked up beyond what a single treatment can solve. It is not for everyone with a few issues. You may be a good fit if any of these describe you:

Your teeth are worn, cracked, or breaking down across the whole mouth

You have multiple missing teeth combined with other issues

Your bite feels off, or you get jaw pain and headaches from clenching

You have years of crowns, fillings, and bridges that keep failing

What Full-Mouth Rehab Restores

When it is done well, a rehabilitation gives you three things back at once, not just a nicer smile:

Function. The ability to bite and chew comfortably on both sides again, without avoiding foods.

Comfort. An even, balanced bite that stops the wear, the clenching pain, and the morning headaches.

Appearance. Teeth designed around your face, shade, and proportion so nothing looks off.

Why It Is Planned as One Case

Most people arrive with quotes from two or three offices for treatments handled separately. The problem with that approach is that the parts of your mouth all affect each other. Your bite depends on the height of your teeth. Your implants depend on healthy gums and enough bone. A crown made without accounting for the bite fails early.

Planning the whole case together is what makes the parts fit and last. Every step is sequenced so it supports the next, gum health before implants, bone before restorations, bite before final teeth. That is what a prosthodontist is trained for and what a coordinated rehabilitation delivers.

Precision-trained, patient-first.


## Why Patients Choose Dr. Meskin for Full-Mouth Rehabilitation


Dr. Meskin is a prosthodontist dedicated to one thing: replacing and restoring teeth so they look, feel, and function like the ones you were born with. He earned his Doctor of Dental Surgery degree and completed his specialty training in prosthodontics at NYU, then refined his implant work as an associate prosthodontist at ClearChoice, one of the largest dental implant networks in the country. Today he leads Hackensack Center for Dental Implants, where every case is planned in 3D, fabricated in an on-site lab, and designed around the patient sitting in front of him. He provides care in English, Spanish, and Russian.

NYU-trained specialist in replacing and restoring teeth.

## What Your Rehabilitation Can Include


Every full-mouth plan is built from the treatments your case actually needs, in an order that makes sense. Here are the components Dr. Meskin most often combines.

Dental Crowns

Custom caps that cover and protect teeth that are cracked, worn, or heavily restored. In full-mouth cases, crowns often rebuild the height of teeth lost to years of grinding and reset your bite at the same time.

Dental Bridges

When several teeth in a row are missing, a bridge closes the span. In a rehab context, bridges are usually supported by implants rather than by grinding down healthy neighboring teeth.

Porcelain Veneers

Thin porcelain shells bonded to the front of teeth that are chipped, discolored, or uneven. Used where the underlying tooth is still sound and the goal is to restore appearance.

Single and Multi-Tooth Implants

Titanium posts that replace missing tooth roots, supporting a single crown or an implant bridge. Implants preserve the bone underneath and become the foundation for the finished restoration.

All-on-X / Full-Arch Implants

When an entire arch needs replacing, four to six implants can support a full fixed set of teeth. Used in rehab cases where all the teeth in one or both jaws are failing.

Bite Correction and Occlusal Therapy

Rebalancing the way your teeth come together, so the load is spread evenly across the arch. Ignoring the bite is why rehabilitation work fails early. Adjusting it is what makes it last.

Gum and Bone Preparation

Treating gum disease, building up bone where it has shrunk, and getting the foundation healthy before restorative work begins. The rest of the plan only holds up on healthy tissue.

Temporary Restorations

Custom temporaries you wear during the months between phases, so you never leave without teeth. They also let us test the shape, length, and bite before anything final is made.

## Your Treatment Journey


Full mouth rehabilitation is delivered in clear, sequenced phases, so you always know where you are and what comes next. Most cases run over a few months to about a year, depending on how much work is needed and how quickly your body heals between phases. Not every step applies to every patient, and Dr. Meskin will tell you which ones your case needs.


### Full Workup and Diagnostics


Your first visit is a thorough evaluation, not a quick look. Dr. Meskin reviews your medical and dental history, examines every tooth, evaluates the health of the gum and bone, and studies how your teeth come together. Because full-mouth cases depend on getting the diagnostics right the first time, this visit covers a lot:

A full clinical exam of teeth, gums, and existing restorations

A 3D cone beam scan of both jaws and the bite

Photographs and impressions to plan the final appearance

A bite and TMJ assessment to see where the load is going wrong

A conversation about your goals, your priorities, and your budget


### Master Plan and Phasing


This is where the case is designed. Using everything from your workup, Dr. Meskin builds a master plan that lists every treatment needed and the order they will happen in. You leave this stage with a clear written plan, a phased timeline, and a firm estimate, with no surprises later.

The plan is sequenced so each step sets up the next. Gum health before implants. Bone before restorations. Bite before final teeth. Skipping that sequence is why so many full-mouth cases done piecemeal fail early.


### Foundation Phase


The foundation phase gets your mouth ready for the finished work. This is where the invisible but essential preparation happens, and it is usually the longest stretch of the plan because healing takes time.

Removing failing teeth that cannot be saved

Treating any active gum disease so the tissue is healthy

Bone grafting where implant sites need building up

Placing the implants that will anchor the restorations

Fitting temporary teeth so you are never without a smile


### Restorative Phase


Once your foundation has healed, the restorative phase rebuilds what you can see. Crowns, veneers, bridges, and implant restorations are placed in the sequence set out in your plan. Because they are built together, they fit together: shade, shape, height, and margin all coordinated from the start rather than one dentist at a time trying to match another.

Temporary restorations are usually worn through this phase so we can test the look and the bite before anything permanent is finalized.


### Finishing, Bite Balance, and Long-Term Care


The final phase is where the whole result is fine-tuned. Dr. Meskin adjusts the bite so the load is spread evenly across the arches, checks that the finished teeth meet exactly as they should, and provides a nightguard if grinding is part of the picture.

From there, the plan shifts into long-term care. Regular check-ins, professional cleanings, and small adjustments over time are what turn a rebuilt mouth into one that keeps working for decades.


## The Rehabilitation Timeline


A full-mouth rehabilitation is not one appointment and a recovery period. It is a phased plan carried out over months, with quiet stretches of healing between the moments when actual work happens. The heaviest days are the ones with surgery, whether extractions, grafts, or implant placement, and those are usually milder than most people expect. Between phases, life is close to normal, with a softer diet at points to protect what is healing underneath.


### A Typical Rehabilitation Timeline



#### Consultation


A single visit, no recovery involved.


#### Foundation phase


3 to 6 months, most of it quiet healing.


#### Restorative phase


Several weeks to a few months, depending on how much is being restored.


#### Finishing and bite balance


Final adjustments across one or two visits.


#### Ongoing care


Check-ins every few months and cleanings twice a year.


## Experience Exceptional Dental Care


If your whole mouth needs attention, book a consultation and see how a coordinated plan can turn it around. At Hackensack Center for Dental Implants, your comfort, your confidence, and your smile always come first.
