## Frequently Asked Questions


How much does full-mouth rehabilitation cost in Hackensack?

It depends entirely on what your mouth needs, since every plan is different. After a full assessment you receive a clear written estimate that lays out each phase, plus financing that can spread it into manageable payments.

How long does the whole process take?

Usually several months, and sometimes up to a year or more for complex cases. The biggest factor is whether implants are involved, since they need time to heal. Your plan comes with a clear timeline up front.

Will I be without teeth during treatment?

No. Provisional teeth keep you eating, speaking, and smiling throughout the process, and they also let you preview your new bite before anything is made permanent.

Why see a prosthodontist for a full-mouth rehabilitation?

This is the core of what a prosthodontist does. Coordinating crowns, implants, bite correction, and appearance into one plan that lasts takes years of specialty training beyond general dentistry. It is Dr. Meskin's daily work.

Can you fix my bite as part of this?

Yes. Correcting a bite that has collapsed or worn down is often central to a rehabilitation, and it is what protects your new teeth from wearing out early.

Do you offer financing?

Yes. We work with Cherry, HFD, Proceed, and CareCredit, and our treatment coordinators will help you find a plan that fits. We also verify any insurance benefits up front.

# Smile Makeovers in Hackensack, NJ


Design the smile you have always wanted, and see it before we ever begin. Dr. Meskin combines the artistry of cosmetic dentistry with the precision of a prosthodontist to create a look that fits your face and feels like you.

JUMP TO SECTION:

Show sections

1. What Is a Smile Makeover?2. Smile Makeovers, Explained3. What a Smile Makeover Can Fix4. Why Us5. What a Smile Makeover Can Include6. Process7. Financing8. FAQs


## What Is a Smile Makeover?


A smile makeover is a personalized plan that combines several cosmetic treatments to transform how your smile looks. Rather than fixing one tooth in isolation, it improves the color, shape, spacing, and balance of your smile as a whole, so the final result looks intentional and natural.

Your makeover might include veneers, teeth whitening, bonding, cosmetic crowns, or clear aligners. What makes it a makeover, and not a list of separate procedures, is that every element is designed together, around your face and your goals.

The real difference is how it starts. Before any permanent work is done, Dr. Meskin designs your new smile and lets you preview it, so you can see, shape, and approve the result first. Nothing is a surprise, because you helped design it.


## Smile Makeovers, Explained


The Benefits of a Smile Makeover

A well-planned smile makeover changes more than the way your teeth look. Patients notice a mix of visible and less visible benefits, from the first reveal and for years afterward:

A natural, coherent smile. Color, shape, length, and gum line all in balance, so nothing looks off or "done."

Designed around your face. Teeth proportioned to your age, lips, and features, not a template.

Renewed confidence. The habit of covering your mouth in photos and conversation quietly disappears.

A single coordinated plan. Multiple treatments sequenced together for one cohesive result, rather than a patchwork.

Who a Smile Makeover Is For

Almost anyone with healthy teeth and gums can benefit from a smile makeover, so this is less about medical eligibility than about whether the treatment fits your goal. You are likely a strong fit if any of these describe you.

You dislike your smile in photos or catch yourself hiding it in conversation

Your teeth are stained, chipped, worn, or uneven

You have gaps, or teeth that look too short or too long

You show more gum than you would like when you smile

Preview Before You Commit

The one question that stops most people from a smile makeover is whether it will end up looking natural. The answer is: not if you see it first.

Cosmetic dentistry now uses two tools that let you preview your new smile before anything permanent happens.

Digital Smile Design. Software overlays a proposed new smile onto photos and video of your face, so tooth size, shape, proportion, and the gum line are evaluated together, including how the smile moves with your lip and speech.

Trial Smile. A tooth-colored composite mockup placed directly over your natural teeth, no drilling required. You wear it in the mirror, take it home, and only when you love it do we move to anything permanent.


## What a Smile Makeover Can Fix


Small things can hold a smile back. A little discoloration, a chip, a gap, teeth that have worn unevenly over the years. On their own each seems minor, but together they are often why someone stops smiling freely. A makeover addresses them as a whole. Here is what it sets right.

Stains and Discoloration

Yellowing, dullness, or stains that no toothpaste will lift, whether from coffee, wine, tobacco, age, or old fillings darkening over time. Professional whitening handles most surface and deeper staining, and it is usually the first step in any makeover plan because natural teeth can be whitened but porcelain veneers cannot. For stains that whitening will not lift, such as tetracycline discoloration or heavily fluorosed teeth, veneers or bonding cover the tooth entirely.

Chips, Cracks, and Gaps

Chipped edges, hairline cracks, or teeth that have worn down over the years, often from grinding. Composite bonding rebuilds small chips in a single visit. Larger chips, visible cracks, or teeth that have lost real length are better rebuilt with porcelain veneers or crowns, which restore the strength as well as the look. If grinding is the cause, we plan a nightguard alongside the cosmetic work so it does not happen again to the new teeth.

Gaps Between Teeth

Small gaps that feel too visible, uneven spacing, or a single wider gap in the front. Bonding closes small gaps quickly and affordably. Porcelain veneers close wider gaps or several at once with a more polished result. When the gap is caused by teeth that have drifted, clear aligner orthodontics is sometimes the better first step, since aligning first often means less veneer coverage later.

Uneven, Worn, or Misshapen Teeth

Teeth that look shorter than they should, that end unevenly, that are slightly crooked, or that have odd shapes. Reshaping the enamel handles small edge irregularities. Bonding or veneers rebuild teeth that have lost length or shape. Where crowding is the underlying cause, we consider whether short-course clear aligners could reset the arch before any restorative work.

A Gummy Smile or an Uneven Gum Line

When your smile shows more gum than you would like, or when the gum line is uneven from tooth to tooth so some teeth look shorter than their neighbors. Gum contouring reshapes the gum with a soft-tissue laser, so more of the tooth shows and the smile line becomes even. Often combined with veneers so the tooth length and gum line are designed together.

Crooked or Crowded Teeth

Mild crowding, rotated teeth, or a smile that has shifted with age. Clear aligners such as Invisalign are usually the least invasive fix. In adults with time constraints, veneers can also visually correct mild misalignment, though for anything beyond mild we recommend aligning first.

Old Crowns and Fillings That No Longer Match

Older crowns with dark margins near the gum, front fillings that have darkened, or restorations that no longer match the teeth around them. Replacing them with newer materials, matched by a prosthodontist and finished in the on-site lab, is often what a smile makeover turns out to actually mean for patients whose natural teeth are otherwise fine.


## Why Patients Choose Dr. Meskin for Their Smile Makeover


Precision-trained, patient-first.

Dr. Meskin is a prosthodontist dedicated to one thing: replacing and restoring teeth so they look, feel, and function like the ones you were born with. He earned his Doctor of Dental Surgery degree and completed his specialty training in prosthodontics at NYU, then refined his implant work as an associate prosthodontist at ClearChoice, one of the largest dental implant networks in the country. Today he leads Hackensack Center for Dental Implants, where every case is planned in 3D, fabricated in an on-site lab, and designed around the patient sitting in front of him. He provides care in English, Spanish, and Russian.

The work speaks through the patients who wear it.

Patients describe him as an artist with a gentle touch whose restorative work looks so natural no one can tell.

## What a Smile Makeover Can Include


Your smile makeover is built from the treatments your case actually needs, in a sequence that makes sense. Here are the components Dr. Meskin most often combines.

Professional Teeth Whitening

The starting point for most makeovers. Natural teeth can be whitened but veneers and crowns cannot, which is why whitening always comes first. Available as in-office whitening, take-home trays, or both, chosen to reach the shade your restorations will be matched to.

Composite Bonding

Tooth-colored resin applied directly to the tooth and shaped by hand to repair chips, close small gaps, smooth uneven edges, or lengthen a short tooth. Done in one visit, no drilling in most cases, and often the most affordable way to make a noticeable change.

Porcelain Veneers

Thin porcelain shells bonded to the front of the teeth to change shape, color, length, or spacing all at once. The most versatile cosmetic option, and the one most people picture when they hear "smile makeover." Custom-designed to match the rest of your face.

Dental Crowns

Full-coverage restorations used when a tooth is heavily damaged, cracked, or has a large old filling that needs replacing. In a makeover, crowns are often placed alongside veneers so the whole smile blends together.

Complete Smile Design

For a full transformation, several treatments are combined into one coordinated plan, designed around your facial proportions for a cohesive, natural result.

Clear Aligners

When teeth need straightening before or as part of a makeover, clear aligners can quietly correct alignment to set the foundation for the final look.

Gum Contouring

For a gummy smile or an uneven gum line, gentle reshaping balances the frame around your teeth, so the whole smile looks even.

Book A Consultation


## Your Treatment Journey


A smile makeover is delivered in clear, planned stages, so you always know where you are and what comes next. Most cases run from a few weeks for a simple plan to a few months for a comprehensive one, including preview and refinement time. Not every step applies to every case, and Dr. Meskin will tell you which ones yours needs.


### Consultation and Goals Conversation


Your first visit is about understanding what you want your smile to look like, not about selling you veneers. Dr. Meskin examines your teeth, gums, and bite, listens to what has been bothering you, and looks at any reference photos you have brought. Because this visit sets the whole plan, it covers a lot:

A clinical exam of your teeth, gums, and bite

Photos and video of your smile in motion, including how it moves when you speak

A discussion of your goals, reference photos, and what a natural version of your best smile could look like

An honest conversation about which treatments will make a real difference and which will not

A written plan, a firm estimate, and a timeline before you commit to anything


### Digital Smile Design


Between visits, Dr. Meskin designs your new smile digitally. Software overlays a proposed version of your teeth onto photos and video of your face, so tooth size, shape, proportion, and the gum line are all evaluated together rather than tooth by tooth. This is where the details that make a smile look natural on your specific face get worked out: how long the teeth should be for your age, how much they should show when you speak, how they should relate to the shape of your lips. You come back to review the design, and nothing is committed to until you approve.


### Trial Smile, the Preview You Can Wear


Once the digital design is approved, we build a physical version. A tooth-colored composite mockup is placed directly over your natural teeth, no drilling required, so you can see and wear the proposed smile in the mirror, in photos, in conversation. This step is what eliminates the "will I like it" fear, because you live in the new smile for a short time before anything permanent happens.

If anything about the length, shape, shade, or overall feel is off, we adjust the design and try again. Only when you are certain do we move to permanent work.


### Treatment


With the design locked in, the actual treatments happen in the sequence set out in your plan. Whitening comes first if it is part of the case, so any restorations can be matched to your final shade. Gum contouring, if needed, happens before veneers so the tooth length is designed to the new gum line. Bonding, veneers, and crowns are placed in the order that makes sense for your case, with temporaries fitted if any tooth needs prep between visits.


### Reveal, Bite Balance, and Follow-Up


The final visit is where the whole smile comes together. Dr. Meskin checks the fit of every restoration, adjusts the bite so the load spreads evenly across your teeth, and polishes the finished result. You leave with the smile you designed together, and we see you back for check-ins to make sure it stays comfortable and looking good.

For patients whose plan included whitening, we agree on a top-up schedule so your natural teeth stay matched to your restorations over time.

Book a consultation and start designing the smile you have always wanted. At Hackensack Center for Dental Implants, your comfort, your confidence, and your smile always come first.

## Frequently Asked Questions


How much does a smile makeover cost in Hackensack?

It depends on which treatments your makeover includes, since every plan is designed individually. After your consultation you receive a clear written estimate, plus financing that can spread it into manageable payments.

Can I really see my new smile before treatment?

Yes, and it is one of the best parts. With a 3D Smile Test Drive, you can preview and try on your future smile before any permanent work begins, and adjust the design until you love it.

Will my smile look natural or fake?

Natural is the whole point. As a prosthodontist, Dr. Meskin designs your smile around your face and features, matching shade, shape, and proportion, so it enhances your look rather than announcing itself.

How long does a smile makeover take?

It depends on the treatments involved. Whitening and bonding can be done in a visit or two, while veneers usually take a few visits. Your timeline is mapped out at your consultation.

Does a smile makeover hurt?

Most cosmetic treatments are gentle, with little to no discomfort. For anything more involved, local anesthetic and sedation options keep you comfortable.

How long will my results last?

With good care, veneers and crowns can last many years, and whitening can be maintained with occasional touch-ups. Dr. Meskin will explain what to expect for your specific plan.

Do you offer financing?

Yes. We work with Cherry, HFD, Proceed, and CareCredit, and our treatment coordinators will help you find a plan that fits. We also verify any benefits up front.

# Emergency Dental Care in Hackensack, NJ


Lost a crown, cracked a tooth, or have a failing implant that suddenly hurts? Dr. Meskin handles urgent restorative and implant problems quickly, so you are not left in pain or panic.

Request an Urgent Appointment

JUMP TO SECTION:

## What Counts as a Dental Emergency?


A dental emergency is any problem that needs fast attention to save a tooth, stop bleeding, or relieve severe pain. These situations cannot wait for a routine appointment, because delay usually turns a small problem into a much bigger one, including permanent tooth loss, spreading infection, or damage that costs many times more to fix later.

At Hackensack Center, we prioritize urgent problems and see them the same day whenever possible. Dr. Meskin is a prosthodontist, which matters here because most true dental emergencies involve broken teeth, failing crowns and bridges, loose or painful implants, or the kind of restorative work a specialist handles best.

If you have terrible tooth pain, a knocked-out tooth, a lost crown, a failing implant, or swelling, request an urgent appointment through the form and describe what happened. Our goal is to get you seen quickly, relieve your pain, and give you a clear plan for what comes next.


## Common Dental Emergencies We Treat in Hackensack


Severe Toothaches

Intense, throbbing tooth pain that gets in the way of eating, sleeping, or daily activities. Often a sign of infection, deep decay, or a cracked tooth. Needs immediate treatment to stop the pain and prevent it from getting worse.

Knocked-Out Teeth

Complete tooth loss from trauma or an accident. This is time-critical, because the tooth can often be saved if replanted within 30 to 60 minutes. Handle it by the crown only, keep it moist in milk or your own saliva, and get to us right away.

Broken or Chipped Teeth

Fractured, cracked, or badly chipped teeth from injury, biting hard objects, or grinding. Sharp edges can cut soft tissue and expose the sensitive inner tooth. Fast repair protects against infection and more damage.

Dental Abscesses

A painful, pus-filled infection at the root or in the gum. Left untreated, an abscess can cause facial swelling, fever, and serious systemic problems. Needs prompt drainage, antibiotics, and treatment of the underlying cause.

Lost Fillings or Crowns

Dental fillings or custom crowns that fall out leave tooth structure exposed and vulnerable to pain, sensitivity, and more damage. Fast replacement prevents the need for bigger (and more expensive) treatment later.

Oral Bleeding

Uncontrolled bleeding from gums, tongue, or other soft tissues that does not stop with pressure. May come from injury, surgery complications, or a hidden condition. Needs professional evaluation and care.


## What to Do Right Now


While you arrange to be seen, a few simple steps can protect your tooth and ease the pain. The most important thing is not to panic, and not to try permanent fixes yourself. Never use household or super glue on a tooth or crown, and never force anything into place.

Once you have done the relevant step below, request an urgent appointment so we can repair it properly.

Lost crown or filling: keep the piece if you can, avoid chewing on that side, and see us soon

Broken or chipped tooth: rinse with warm water, save any fragments, use a cold compress for swelling

Knocked-out tooth: handle it by the crown only, keep it in milk or saliva, and get seen within the hour

Loose or painful implant: avoid chewing on it and have it assessed quickly to protect the bone

Swelling or a gum abscess: rinse gently with warm salt water and be seen urgently, do not try to drain it

Severe pain: an over-the-counter pain reliever can help until you are seen

These are airway and systemic concerns a hospital is equipped to manage. For everything else, a specialist is the faster path to real relief.

## How Your Emergency Visit Works


Emergency visits at Hackensack Center are focused: relieve the pain or bleeding first, figure out what actually happened, and stabilize the tooth so you leave in better shape than you arrived. Whether the fix is complete on the same day or requires a follow-up depends on what we find.


### Relieve


Comfort comes first. Before anything else, we numb the area, control any bleeding, and get you out of pain. If you are anxious, we can talk through sedation options as well. Nothing else happens until you are comfortable.


### Diagnose


Once you are settled, Dr. Meskin figures out what is going on. That usually includes an exam, targeted x-rays, and where needed a 3D scan to see below the gum. Because most emergencies are not just what they look like on the surface, this step is what separates a real fix from a temporary patch. A tooth that hurts might be cracked, infected, or bearing force it should not be. The diagnosis decides the treatment.


### Stabilize or Repair


Where possible, we complete the repair the same day. Because we have an on-site lab, temporary crowns and same-day restorations are often finished before you leave. In cases where a proper fix takes more than one visit, such as an implant that needs to be removed and rebuilt, we stabilize the site, protect the tooth, and plan the definitive treatment in the following days.


### What Happens Next


Before you leave, you receive clear aftercare instructions and a plan for anything that still needs to be done. Many emergency fixes are the first step of a longer treatment. A saved tooth may still need a root canal. A re-cemented crown may need to be remade. A stabilized implant may need a new restoration. We tell you exactly what is next and when.


## Preventing Dental Emergencies


Many dental emergencies can be prevented with proper care, protective measures, and regular dental visits at our Hackensack, NJ practice.

Maintain Excellent Oral Hygiene

Brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste, floss every day, and keep up with regular professional cleanings and exams at Hackensack Center. Many emergencies, including abscesses, severe decay, and tooth fractures, come from untreated problems that could have been caught early.

Wear Protective Mouthguards

If you play contact sports, do activities with fall risk, or grind your teeth at night, wear a custom mouthguard. A professionally fitted sports guard or nightguard from Hackensack Center gives much better protection than a store-bought one.

Avoid Risky Habits

Do not use your teeth as tools to open packages, crack nuts, or hold objects. Avoid chewing ice, hard candy, and popcorn kernels. These habits put unnecessary stress on teeth and raise your emergency risk.

Address Problems Early

Do not ignore small dental issues hoping they will go away. A small cavity or minor sensitivity can quickly turn into a painful emergency. Schedule an appointment at the first sign of trouble.


## Experience Exceptional Dental Care


If dental work has failed or you are in pain, request an urgent appointment and we will get you seen as quickly as we safely can. At Hackensack Center for Dental Implants, your comfort comes first.


## Frequently Asked Questions


Do you offer same-day emergency appointments?

We make every effort to see urgent problems as quickly as possible. Request an appointment through the form and describe what happened, and we will arrange the soonest visit we can.

My crown fell off. Is that an emergency?

It is urgent, even without pain, because the tooth underneath is now exposed and vulnerable. Keep the crown, avoid chewing on that side, and request an appointment soon so we can re-secure or remake it.

I think my implant is loose. What should I do?

Have it assessed quickly. A loose or painful implant can worsen and cost you bone if left. Acting early often means more of the implant can be saved.

What should I do with a knocked-out tooth?

Handle it by the crown, not the root, keep it moist in milk or your own saliva, and try to be seen within the hour, which gives it the best chance of being saved.

When should I go to the ER instead of a dentist?

Go to the ER for trouble breathing or swallowing, swelling spreading toward your eye or neck, or bleeding that will not stop after 15 minutes of firm pressure. For most other dental emergencies, a dentist is the faster route to relief.

Can I just glue my crown back on?

No. Household and super glues are toxic and can damage the tooth and make a proper repair harder. Keep the crown and let us re-secure it correctly.

Do you offer financing for emergency treatment?

Yes. We work with Cherry, HFD, Proceed, and CareCredit, and our treatment coordinators will help you find a plan that fits. We also verify any insurance benefits.

# Dr. Alan Meskin, Prosthodontist and Implant Specialist


NYU-trained and focused entirely on replacing and restoring teeth, Dr. Alan Meskin specializes in dental implants, full-mouth reconstruction, and cosmetic smile design, including the complex cases other offices refer out.


## Meet Dr. Meskin


Dr. Alan Meskin is a prosthodontist, a dental specialist trained specifically in replacing and restoring teeth. He earned his Doctor of Dental Surgery from NYU College of Dentistry in 2019, then completed a further certificate in prosthodontics at NYU in 2022, focusing on implant restoration and full-mouth reconstruction. Dr. Meskin describes himself simply: a prosthodontist dedicated to smile design and full-mouth rehabilitation, with a focus on implant prosthetics. That focus is deliberate. By concentrating on replacing and restoring teeth rather than spreading across every area of dentistry, he is able to bring real depth to the cases that need it most.

His work centers on one goal: rebuilding smiles so naturally that no one can tell. Patients describe him as gentle and thorough, a dentist who takes the time to explain, listens first, and puts anxious patients at ease. He provides care in English, Spanish, and Russian. His philosophy is patient-first and detail-driven. Every plan begins by listening to what the patient actually wants, and every restoration is designed to look and function like a natural tooth. He is committed to continuing education, regularly taking courses and bringing the newest techniques in digital and implant dentistry back to his patients.

Full-mouth reconstruction and rehabilitation

Cosmetic smile design and makeovers

# About Hackensack Center for Dental Implants


Hackensack Center for Dental Implants is a specialist practice built around one focus: replacing and restoring teeth exceptionally well. Led by prosthodontist Dr. Alan Meskin, we combine advanced technology, an on-site lab, and genuinely personal care to rebuild smiles that look natural and last.

Dr. Alan Meskin built this practice on a simple idea: that rebuilding a smile is as much about the person as the teeth. As a prosthodontist, he completed years of specialty training at NYU focused entirely on replacing and restoring teeth, and he has devoted his career to the work a lot of general offices refer out, from full-arch implants to complex, full-mouth reconstruction.

That experience adds up. Three decades of implant and reconstructive work, with thousands of implants placed and over 1,000 full-arch cases completed. Every one of them was planned in 3D before it began, and the teeth themselves were designed and crafted in our own on-site lab, so nothing gets shipped out and lost in a handoff. It means fewer visits, tighter quality control, and a result made to fit your face rather than pulled from a catalog.

Just as important is how the practice feels. Many of the people who come to us have put off care for years, often because a past experience left them anxious or embarrassed. We built the opposite of that: a calm, judgment-free place on Main Street where questions are welcome, comfort comes first, and care is offered in English, Spanish, and Russian.

Our pledge is straightforward. We will help you understand your options honestly, plan the path that genuinely fits your needs and your budget, and stay with you from the first consultation to the final smile. Thank you for visiting, and we look forward to meeting you.

-Dr. Alan Meskin


## Exceptional Doctors, Extraordinary Care


Complex implant cases are rarely a one-person job. Our team brings together a prosthodontist, two oral and maxillofacial surgeons, and a periodontist, each trained at a top dental school and each focused on a different part of your treatment. You get specialist-level care at every stage, coordinated under one roof, without being sent across town between offices.

Dr. Alan Meskin

Dr. Alan Meskin is a prosthodontist, an NYU-trained specialist in implant restoration and full-mouth reconstruction, and the specialist behind every case here.

More About Dr. Meskin

Dr. Maurice Srour

NYU-trained oral and maxillofacial surgeon specializing in surgical implant placement, bone grafting, and complex extractions.

More About Dr. Srour

Dr. Won-Sang Lee

Columbia-trained oral and maxillofacial surgeon specializing in extractions, corrective jaw surgery, and implant placement.

More About Dr. Lee

Dr. Dmitriy Klass

NYU and Boston University-trained periodontist and implant surgeon specializing in bone and gum grafting and minimally invasive periodontal care.

More About Dr. Klass


## The Technology Behind Better Implant Results


Precision is what separates an implant that lasts decades from one that fails early. Every case here is planned digitally before any treatment begins, which means fewer surprises, fewer appointments, and a result that fits the way it was designed to.

Cone Beam 3D Imaging

Digital X-rays

Intraoral Scanners

3D Printing

CAD/CAM Design

A three-dimensional scan of your jaw that shows exactly where the bone is, where the nerves and sinuses sit, and where each implant can be placed safely. This is where your treatment is planned, before anything else happens.

Detailed images captured in seconds with significantly less radiation than traditional film. Dr. Meskin can show you what he sees on screen during your visit, so you understand your diagnosis rather than just hearing it.

A small handheld scanner takes a precise digital impression of your mouth without the mess of putty trays. Faster, far more comfortable, and accurate down to the detail your final teeth depend on.

Surgical guides, models, and provisional teeth printed in-house in our own lab. It is what allows us to place implants exactly where they were planned and hand you a new smile the same day.

CAD/CAM

Your new teeth are designed digitally, down to the shape, shade, and how they meet your bite, then produced with computer-guided precision rather than by hand. It is what lets us match a result to your face instead of pulling from a catalog.

Explore Our Technology


## WHY CHOOSE HACKENSACK CENTERfor DENTAL IMPLANTS


We are a specialist practice, not a general office that also does implants. That difference shows up in how your case is planned, who performs your treatment, and how you are treated while you are here.


### Decades of Combined Experience


Three decades of implant and reconstructive work, with thousands of implants placed and over 1,000 full-arch cases completed. This is advanced specialty care from people who do it every day, not occasionally.


### Specialist-Led at Every Stage


Your surgery is performed by an oral surgeon or periodontist. Your restoration is designed and finished by a prosthodontist. You are never handed to a generalist for the part that matters most.


### Our Own On-Site Lab


Your teeth are designed and crafted in our own lab, in the same building, by a technician who works directly with Dr. Meskin. That means fewer visits, tighter control over the result, and adjustments made in hours rather than weeks.


### Comprehensive Care Under One Roof


Implants, full-mouth rehabilitation, periodontal treatment, oral surgery, Invisalign, and routine hygiene. Whatever your mouth needs, it is handled here, by our own team.


### Care in Three Languages


Dr. Meskin and our team provide care in English, Spanish, and Russian, so you can ask questions and understand your options in the language you think in.


### Sedation for Anxious Patients


A full range of sedation options is available, up to IV sedation. If fear is the reason you have been putting off care, tell us when you book and we will plan around it.


### Flexible Financing


We will find a way. We work with Cherry, CareCredit, Proceed, and HFD, and our treatment coordinators will help you find a plan that fits your budget.


### A TV in Every Room


every treatment room has its own TV for longer appointments


### Aromatherapy Throughout the Office


No clinical smell. Aromatherapy runs throughout the office, so walking in does not immediately remind you of every appointment you have been dreading.

Request an Appointment and Start Your Smile Journey Today.

Schedule your consultation today and see how different dental care can feel. At Hackensack Center for Dental Implants, your comfort, your confidence, and your smile are always our priority.


## Frequently Asked Questions


What makes Hackensack Center different?

We are a specialist practice focused on implants and restorative dentistry, led by a prosthodontist, with an on-site lab and care in three languages. That combination is unusual, and it is what lets us take on the complex cases many general offices refer out.

What is a prosthodontist?

A prosthodontist is a dental specialist who completed years of additional training beyond dental school, focused specifically on replacing and restoring teeth. For implants, full-arch work, and cosmetic reconstruction, that specialization means more predictable, natural-looking results.

Do you only do implants?

No. Implants are our primary focus, but Dr. Meskin also does full-mouth reconstruction and cosmetic smile makeovers. Whatever your smile needs, it can be handled under one roof.

Where are you located?

We are at 163 Main Street, Suite A, in Hackensack, serving the greater Bergen County area.

Do you offer financing?

Yes. We work with Cherry, HFD, Proceed, and CareCredit, and our treatment coordinators will help you find a plan that fits. We also verify any insurance benefits up front.

# Insurance and Financing in Hackensack, NJ


Cost should never stand between you and the care you need. We work with every financing option available to you, and our treatment coordinators will help you find a plan that fits your budget.


## Finance Options Available, for Your Dental Treatments


We believe a healthy, confident smile should be within reach, whatever your situation. In the doctor's own words, we will find a way. We try every avenue, and our dedicated team of treatment coordinators will sit down with you to walk through your options until we land on a plan that works.

Get treatment now

Pay off at any time

Flexible deposits

Split the cost


## Our Financing Partners


Cherry Payment Plans

Cherry is one of the most popular healthcare financing options, built specifically for dental and medical care. You can apply in minutes with a soft credit check that does not affect your score, and qualified applicants can access 0% APR plans with no deferred interest. Payment terms range from 3 to 60 months.

Key Features:

Soft credit check, no impact to apply

0% APR for qualifying applicants, no deferred interest

Plans from 3 to 60 months

Fast online application with a quick decision

Healthcare Finance Direct

HFD focuses on making larger treatment plans manageable, with flexible structures designed to fit a range of budgets and credit situations. Our coordinators can walk you through whether HFD is the right fit for your treatment.

Options for a range of credit profiles

Flexible terms for larger cases

Guided by our treatment coordinators

Proceed Finance

Proceed specializes in financing larger and more comprehensive dental cases, such as full-arch and full-mouth treatment, with longer installment options and true 0% APR plans for those who qualify.

Built for larger, comprehensive cases

Longer-term installment options

0% APR options for qualifying applicants

CareCredit

CareCredit is a long-established healthcare credit card offering promotional no-interest periods when the balance is paid in full within the promotional window. Our coordinators will explain the terms clearly, so you know exactly how the promotional period works before you commit.

Widely accepted healthcare financing

Promotional no-interest periods when paid in full on time

Soft credit check option to apply

Request an appointment


## Not Sure What Your Insurance Actually Covers?


Insurance can be confusing, especially when it comes to implants, crowns, and restorative work. Our team verifies your benefits, explains what your plan actually pays, and gives you a clear estimate up front, before any treatment begins.

Benefits Verified Up Front. Before any treatment starts, we review your plan and confirm your coverage in advance, so you know exactly what insurance will pay and what you will owe. No surprise bills after the fact.

Every Dollar of Coverage Used. Insurance rarely covers the full cost of implant or restorative work, but it often covers more than people expect. Our coordinators handle the paperwork and claims for you and make sure you get every dollar of the benefit you are entitled to.

Combined with Financing. Where insurance covers only part, financing bridges the rest. We help you combine the two so your care stays affordable, and we flag any unused annual benefits before they expire at year end.

Verify My Benefits


## Answering Your Questions About Insurance and Financing


Do I need good credit to qualify?

Not necessarily. Our partners offer soft credit checks so you can see what you qualify for without any impact on your score. Cherry, for example, considers applicants with credit scores as low as 520. If one partner is not the right fit, our coordinators can often find another that is.

Will applying affect my credit score?

No, not at the application stage. All four of our financing partners offer soft credit checks to see your options, which do not affect your score. A hard check only happens later, if and when you formally accept a plan.

How much can I finance?

It depends on the partner and your qualification, but our partners cover treatments from smaller single-tooth cases through full-mouth reconstruction. For larger cases like full-arch implants, Proceed Finance is specifically built for higher amounts.

What are the monthly payments like?

Monthly payments depend on your treatment cost, your term length, and your qualification. Longer terms mean lower monthly payments. Our coordinators will run the numbers with you before you commit, so there are no surprises.

Do you take my dental insurance?

We work with most dental insurance plans and verify your benefits before treatment. Even if we are out of network, many plans still cover part of your care, and our coordinators handle the paperwork for you.

Can I combine insurance and financing?

Yes, and it is often the smartest approach. Insurance covers part of the treatment, financing covers the rest, and your out-of-pocket cost is spread across manageable monthly payments.

What if I still cannot afford it?

Talk to us anyway. In the doctor's own words, we will find a way. Our coordinators work through every avenue, from combining plans to phasing your treatment, so cost does not become the reason you go without care.

# First Visit Expectations


Your first visit is a relaxed, no-pressure conversation and exam, not a hard sell. Here is exactly what to expect, so there are no surprises when you walk in.

Your first visit is not only about our team getting to know you, but about you getting to know us too. In the time we spend together, we want you to ask questions, share what has been on your mind, and tell us anything you want us to know that will help make your care fit you specifically.

Part of getting to know you means reviewing your medical history in detail. Certain conditions and medications can affect implant healing and treatment planning, so you will be asked for a list of your medications and dosages, including vitamins and supplements. This is not paperwork for the sake of paperwork. It is how we keep your care safe.

A comprehensive oral exam is performed, along with digital x-rays and, where the case calls for it, a 3D cone beam scan. If it has been a while since your last dental visit, do not worry about it. You have made the decision to come in, which is the part that matters.

Once the exam is complete, Dr. Meskin walks you through what he sees, in plain language, on the same screen you are looking at. Together you build a treatment plan that fits your dental needs and your life, phased and paced in a way you can afford. You leave with a written estimate and a clear plan, not with pressure to commit.

Above all, we want you to feel comfortable, physically and emotionally. That is not a marketing line. It is the whole point of a first visit at Hackensack Center.


## Specialist Care From the First Appointment.


At Hackensack Center, every part of your visit is designed around one thing: giving you specialist-level implant and restorative care in an office that actually feels calm. Dr. Meskin plans and delivers your treatment personally, from the first scan to the final restoration.


### NYU-Trained Prosthodontist


Dr. Meskin earned his dental degree and his prosthodontics specialty at NYU.


### On-Site Dental Lab


Your crown, bridge, or full-arch restoration is designed and finished in-house, so Dr. Meskin and the lab technician work together on your case rather than shipping it out and hoping the fit comes back right.


### Every Case Planned in 3D


Every implant and restorative case is planned against a cone beam CT scan of your jaw. Better diagnostics means fewer surprises and more predictable results.


### Same-Day Temporary Teeth


For full-arch cases, most patients leave surgery with a fixed set of temporary teeth the same day. You are never sent home with a visible gap.


### Sedation Available


If dental anxiety is a concern, tell us. We offer a full range of sedation options, up to IV sedation, so your comfort is not a limiting factor in your care.


### Flexible Financing


We will find a way. Our coordinators help you build a plan that fits your budget, with financing through Cherry, HFD, Proceed, and CareCredit.


### Care in Three Languages


Dr. Meskin cares for patients in English, Spanish, and Russian, so you can discuss your treatment comfortably in your own words.


### Second Opinions Welcome


Many first visits at Hackensack Center are second opinions. If you were quoted a big treatment plan somewhere else, or told an implant could not be saved, come in for an honest specialist review before you commit.


### Start Your Journey to Better Dental Health Today


Request an Appointment and Start Your Smile Journey Today.

At our practice, we see beauty and oral health as inseparable. Our dedication to health, inspired by the art of creating beautiful smiles, is at the heart of our success.


## It’s a whole new experience.



## Watch Our Patient Video Diaries


Hear the real stories of patients who were right where you are, in their own words.

View All Testimonials


## Experience Exceptional Dental Care


If an implant has let you down, book a consultation and get an honest, specialist opinion on what can be done. At Hackensack Center for Dental Implants, your comfort, your confidence, and your smile always come first.


## Frequently Asked Questions


What should I expect at my first visit?

Your first visit is focused on understanding what brought you in and building the right plan. Dr. Alan Meskin will review your concerns and goals, evaluate your oral health, review your health history, and use appropriate diagnostic imaging to understand your case before recommending treatment.

What should I bring to my first appointment?

Please bring a current list of your medications and dosages, including vitamins and supplements. If you already have recent dental records or imaging from another office, bringing those can also help the team understand your history and avoid unnecessary repetition.

Will I get a 3D scan at my first visit?

For implant and restorative cases, treatment planning is based on cone beam CT imaging of your jaw. This 3D information helps Dr. Meskin evaluate the area carefully and plan treatment with fewer surprises and more predictable results.

Will I meet with Dr. Alan Meskin personally?

Yes. Dr. Meskin personally plans and delivers treatment at Hackensack Center, so your first visit is built around a direct specialist evaluation and a treatment plan designed for your specific needs.

Can I come in for a second opinion?

Absolutely. Many first visits at Hackensack Center are second opinions. If you were given a large treatment plan elsewhere or told an implant could not be saved, Dr. Meskin can review the situation and give you a specialist perspective before you commit.

Will I receive a treatment plan at my first visit?

After your evaluation and diagnostic review, the team will explain the findings, appropriate treatment options, and recommended next steps. More complex cases may require additional planning before every detail of the final treatment plan is confirmed.

Can we review costs, insurance, and financing at my first visit?

Yes. Once the recommended options are clear, the team can review estimated treatment costs, available insurance benefits, and financing options so you understand the financial side before deciding how to move forward.

# TERMS AND CONDITIONS


Effective Date: September 21, 2026

These Terms and Conditions (“Terms”) govern your use of the website operated by Aesthetic Dental Center of Hackensack, LLC DBA Hackensack Center for Dental Implants (“Hackensack Center for Dental Implants,” “we,” “us,” or “our”), located at https://www.hackensackdentalimplants.com/ (the “Site”), as well as our text messaging program and related electronic services.

By accessing or using the Site, submitting information through a form, requesting a consultation or appointment, opting in to receive text messages, or otherwise communicating with us electronically, you agree to these Terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the Site or our online services.

We may revise these Terms periodically. Revised Terms will be posted on this page with an updated Effective Date.


## 1. ABOUT US


The Site is operated by:

Aesthetic Dental Center of Hackensack, LLC

DBA Hackensack Center for Dental Implants

163 Main Street, Suite A1

Hackensack, NJ 07601

References to “Hackensack Center,” “we,” “us,” and “our” mean this entity. References to “you” and “your” mean the individual using the Site or our services.


## 2. ELIGIBILITY AND ACCEPTABLE USE


You must be at least 18 years old, or use the Site with the involvement and permission of a parent or legal guardian, to submit information, request a consultation, schedule an appointment, or enroll in our text messaging program.

You agree to use the Site only for lawful purposes and in a manner that does not interfere with its operation, security, or availability.

You may not:

Submit false information or another person’s information without authorization.

Enroll a telephone number you do not own or are not authorized to use.

Impersonate another person or misrepresent your relationship with an individual or organization.

Attempt to access accounts, systems, or information you are not authorized to access.

Use bots, scrapers, or other automated systems to harvest information or submit forms.

Introduce malware or otherwise disrupt the operation or security of the Site.

Collect or store personal information about another user without authorization.

Use Site content to advertise or promote another business without written permission.


## 3. INFORMATIONAL PURPOSE; NO DOCTOR-PATIENT RELATIONSHIP


The Site provides general information about Hackensack Center for Dental Implants, dental implants, prosthodontics, oral surgery, restorative and cosmetic dentistry, treatment options, financing, and related patient resources.

Site content is provided for general informational and educational purposes only. It is not dental or medical advice, a diagnosis, or a treatment plan and should not be used as a substitute for an examination by a licensed healthcare professional.

Viewing the Site, submitting a form, requesting a consultation, exchanging text messages or email, or speaking with a staff member does not create a doctor-patient relationship. A doctor-patient relationship begins only after you have been accepted as a patient and the relationship has been appropriately documented.

If you believe you are experiencing a medical or dental emergency, including uncontrolled bleeding, difficulty breathing, rapidly increasing facial swelling, or another potentially life-threatening condition, call 911 or seek emergency care. Do not rely on website forms, email, or text messages for emergency assistance.


## 4. CONSULTATION AND APPOINTMENT REQUESTS


The Site may allow you to request a consultation or appointment, submit a contact form, complete a virtual-consultation questionnaire, or communicate with our office.

Submitting a request does not guarantee an appointment or establish a treatment relationship. An appointment is confirmed only after our office or scheduling provider verifies availability and contacts you.

You agree to provide accurate, current, and complete information. We may modify, reschedule, or decline requests because of provider availability, scheduling conflicts, emergencies, incomplete information, clinical considerations, or other reasonable circumstances.


## 5. SENSITIVE INFORMATION AND ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATIONS


General website forms, ordinary email, and SMS text messages are intended for routine questions, scheduling, and other non-urgent communications.

Please do not use these channels to send detailed medical or dental histories, clinical records, diagnostic images, government identifiers, payment-card information, financial account information, or other highly sensitive information.

When clinical records, photographs, imaging, or other sensitive information are required, use only a secure method provided or approved by our office.

Electronic communications may be delayed, intercepted, misdirected, or viewed by someone with access to your device or account. Please consider these risks before communicating electronically.

Information created or maintained in connection with your care may constitute protected health information under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (“HIPAA”) and applicable New Jersey law. Such information is also governed by our separate Notice of Privacy Practices. If that notice conflicts with these Terms concerning protected health information, the Notice of Privacy Practices controls.


## 6. PHONE, EMAIL, AND SMS COMMUNICATIONS


By providing contact information through the Site, requesting an appointment, or otherwise communicating with us, you authorize us to respond using the contact methods you provide.

Communications may include responses to inquiries, appointment confirmations and reminders, rescheduling notices, treatment preparation and follow-up information, billing or insurance communications, and other practice-related messages.


### Hackensack Center SMS Program


Hackensack Center for Dental Implants operates an SMS/MMS text messaging program using third-party messaging platforms and telecommunications providers. Messages sent through this program may constitute Application-to-Person (“A2P”) messaging.


### How You Opt In


You may opt in by:

Entering your mobile number, checking the separate SMS-consent checkbox on a Site form, and submitting the form.

Affirmatively agreeing in writing or electronically to receive text messages.

Using another opt-in method clearly presented by Hackensack Center.

Consent to receive marketing or promotional text messages is not a condition of purchasing a product, receiving treatment, or obtaining services.

By affirmatively opting in, you consent to receive recurring automated and conversational SMS or MMS messages from Hackensack Center for Dental Implants at the mobile number you provide. You represent that you own or are authorized to use that number.

Your consent applies only to communications from Hackensack Center for Dental Implants and may not be sold or transferred to another business.


### Types of Messages


Depending on the consent you provide, messages may include:

Appointment messages: Consultation requests, confirmations, reminders, rescheduling notices, preparation information, and follow-up instructions.

Conversational messages: Two-way replies from our staff regarding your inquiry, appointment, or care.

Patient-service messages: Insurance, billing, financing, and care-coordination communications.

Marketing messages: Educational campaigns, special offers, new services, events, and other practice news when you have consented to receive them.


### Message Frequency


Message frequency varies based on your appointments, requests, consent, and interactions with us.


### Message and Data Rates


Message and data rates may apply according to your mobile carrier and plan. Hackensack Center does not charge a separate fee for its text messages.


### How to Opt Out


You may cancel SMS messages at any time by replying STOP to a message from us. We may send one final message confirming your opt-out. After that confirmation, we will stop sending messages covered by your opt-out unless you later provide new consent.

Your SMS opt-out does not prevent us from contacting you through another method when permitted by law, including when reasonably necessary for treatment, payment, healthcare operations, or responding to a communication you initiate.


### How to Get Help


Reply HELP for assistance, call (201) 488-8866, or visit:

https://www.hackensackdentalimplants.com/contact


### Carrier Disclaimer


Wireless carriers are not responsible for delayed or undelivered messages. Message delivery is subject to wireless-network availability and the operation of third-party messaging providers.


### Mobile Information and Privacy


We do not sell or rent your mobile number, SMS opt-in data, or messaging consent.

We do not share mobile information—including telephone numbers, opt-in data, or consent—with third parties or affiliates for their own marketing or promotional purposes.

# Cookie Policy


Last updated: January 1, 2026

This Cookie Policy explains how Hackensack Center for Dental Implants ("Company," "we," "us," and "our") uses cookies and similar technologies to recognize you when you visit our website ("Website"). It explains what these technologies are and why we use them, as well as your rights to control our use of them.

In some cases we may use cookies to collect personal information, or information that becomes personal information if we combine it with other information.


### What Are Cookies?


Cookies are small data files that are placed on your computer or mobile device when you visit a website. Cookies are widely used by website owners in order to make their websites work, or to work more efficiently, as well as to provide reporting information.

Cookies set by the website owner (in this case, Hackensack Center for Dental Implants) are called "first-party cookies." Cookies set by parties other than the website owner are called "third-party cookies." Third-party cookies enable third-party features or functionality to be provided on or through the website (for example, advertising, interactive content, and analytics). The parties that set these third-party cookies can recognize your computer both when it visits the website in question and also when it visits certain other websites.


### Why Do We Use Cookies?


We use first-party and third-party cookies for several reasons. Some cookies are required for technical reasons in order for our Website to operate, and we refer to these as "essential" or "strictly necessary" cookies. Other cookies enable us to understand how visitors use our Website and to improve their experience. Third parties may serve cookies through our Website for analytics and other purposes, as described in more detail below.


### How Can I Control Cookies?


You have the right to decide whether to accept or reject cookies. You can exercise your cookie preferences through the Cookie Consent Manager on our Website, which allows you to select which categories of cookies you accept or reject. Essential cookies cannot be rejected as they are strictly necessary to provide you with services.

If you choose to reject non-essential cookies, you may still use our Website, though your access to some functionality and areas may be restricted. You may also set or amend your web browser controls to accept or refuse cookies.


### Types of Cookies We Use


The specific cookies served through our Website fall into the following categories:

Essential cookies. These cookies are strictly necessary to provide you with services available through our Website and to use some of its features, such as access to secure areas. Without these cookies, services you have asked for cannot be provided.

Analytics and performance cookies. These cookies collect information about how visitors use our Website, such as which pages are visited most often and whether visitors encounter any errors. The information is used in aggregate form to help us understand how the Website is being used and how we can improve it. Common examples include cookies set by Google Analytics.

Functionality cookies. These cookies allow the Website to remember choices you make (such as your language preference) and provide enhanced, more personal features.

Advertising and targeting cookies. These cookies may be set through our Website by advertising partners. They may be used to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant content on our Website or other websites. They do not directly store personal information but are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device.


### How Can I Control Cookies on My Browser?


The means by which you can refuse cookies through your web browser controls vary from browser to browser, so you should visit your browser's help menu for more information. Here is where to find cookie settings in the most popular browsers:

Chrome

Firefox

Safari

Edge

Opera

Internet Explorer

In addition, most advertising networks offer you a way to opt out of targeted advertising. To learn more, please visit:

Digital Advertising Alliance

Digital Advertising Alliance of Canada

European Interactive Digital Advertising Alliance


### What About Other Tracking Technologies, Like Web Beacons?


Cookies are not the only way to recognize or track visitors to a website. We may use other, similar technologies from time to time, like web beacons (sometimes called "tracking pixels" or "clear gifs"). These are tiny graphics files that contain a unique identifier that enables us to recognize when someone has visited our Website or opened an email including them. This allows us to monitor traffic patterns, understand whether you have come to our Website from an online advertisement, improve site performance, and measure the success of email campaigns. In many instances, these technologies rely on cookies to function properly, so declining cookies may impair their functioning.


### Do You Use Flash Cookies or Local Shared Objects?


Websites may also use "Flash Cookies" (also known as Local Shared Objects or "LSOs") to collect and store information about your use of our services and for other site operations.

If you do not want Flash Cookies stored on your device, you can adjust the settings of your Flash player to block Flash Cookies storage using the tools available in the Website Storage Settings Panel. Please note that setting the Flash Player to restrict or limit acceptance of Flash Cookies may reduce or impede the functionality of some Flash applications.


### Do You Serve Targeted Advertising?


Third parties may serve cookies on your computer or mobile device to serve advertising through our Website. These companies may use information about your visits to this and other websites in order to provide relevant advertisements about goods and services that may be of interest to you. They may also use this information to measure the effectiveness of advertisements. The information collected through this process does not enable us or them to identify your name, contact details, or other details that directly identify you unless you choose to provide these.


### How Often Will You Update This Cookie Policy?


We may update this Cookie Policy from time to time in order to reflect changes to the cookies we use or for other operational, legal, or regulatory reasons. Please revisit this Cookie Policy regularly to stay informed about our use of cookies and related technologies.

The date at the top of this Cookie Policy indicates when it was last updated.


### Where Can I Get Further Information?


If you have any questions about our use of cookies or other technologies, please contact us through the form on our Contact page, or by post at:

# Sedation Dentistry in Hackensack, NJ


For patients who have put off dental care because of fear, sensitivity, or a rough experience in the past. Comfortable, monitored sedation, so treatment finally feels manageable.


## What Is Sedation Dentistry?


Sedation dentistry helps you feel calm, relaxed, and at ease during dental procedures. It uses medication to reduce anxiety and sensitivity, so the appointment feels manageable rather than overwhelming. Depending on the level chosen, you may stay fully awake and simply feel relaxed, drift into a semi-conscious "twilight" state, or sleep through the whole procedure entirely.

What sedation is not is a shortcut. It is not a replacement for careful, gentle care, and it does not skip any part of the treatment. What it does is take the fear, the tension, and often the memory of the difficult parts out of the experience, so you can get the care you need without dread.

At Hackensack Center, sedation is available for anyone who wants it. For some patients, it is what finally makes long-avoided care possible.


## What Dental Anxiety Feels Like, and How Sedation Helps


Dental anxiety is common, and there is no reason to be embarrassed by it. For a lot of our patients, the fear is the hardest part of coming in, and sedation is what finally makes it possible. Here is how it changes the experience.

It Quiets the Fear – Anxiety before an appointment can be worse than the appointment itself. Sedation calms the nervous system, so you arrive and stay relaxed rather than tense.

It Takes Out the Memory – The medications we use produce a mild amnesic effect, so much of the procedure simply feels like a hazy blur afterward. For many patients, that alone changes everything.

It Helps Where Numbing Struggles – Some patients are difficult to fully numb, or feel every sensation despite local anesthetic. Sedation adds a second layer of comfort, so treatment is truly painless.

It Lets Us Do More in One Visit – Because you are relaxed for the full appointment, we can complete more treatment at once rather than breaking it into short visits. Fewer appointments, faster progress.


## Types of Sedation We Offer


Oral Conscious Sedation

The mildest option. You take a prescription sedative pill before your appointment, often one the night before to help you sleep and another the morning of. You stay awake and responsive, but deeply relaxed throughout the procedure. Well-suited to shorter appointments and moderate anxiety.

IV Sedation

A stronger, more precise level of sedation delivered intravenously. It places you in a semi-conscious "twilight" state, so you are unaware of the procedure and often will not remember it afterward. IV sedation also reduces post-operative swelling and discomfort, which makes it a good fit for implant surgery and longer visits.

General Anesthesia

The deepest level of sedation, administered by a specially trained dental anesthesiologist. You are fully asleep throughout the procedure and wake up with the treatment complete. General anesthesia is typically used for the most complex or full-arch cases, and for patients who prefer to be entirely unconscious for their care.


## How Your Sedation Appointment Works


Sedation is planned carefully in advance, so nothing about the appointment feels rushed or uncertain.


### Pre-Sedation Consultation


Before we sedate you for anything, Dr. Meskin reviews your health history, current medications, and allergies to confirm which sedation level is right for you. Some medical conditions may require clearance from your physician, and we will let you know if that applies.


### Pre-Appointment Instructions


You receive clear, specific instructions covering fasting, medications, clothing, and transportation. Following these correctly is what makes the sedation both safe and comfortable, so we walk through them with you.


### Sedation Administration


On the day of the procedure, sedation is administered by Dr. Meskin or, for general anesthesia and IV sedation, by our dental anesthesiologist. You are then eased into a calm, comfortable state before treatment begins.


### Monitored Treatment


Throughout the procedure, your vital signs are monitored continuously by trained staff. This is the standard for any level of sedation above oral, and it is how we keep the experience safe as well as comfortable.


### Recovery and Discharge


After treatment, you rest in our recovery area until you are fully alert and stable. You will need a responsible adult to drive you home and stay with you for a few hours, since the effects of sedation can linger for the rest of the day.


## Who Might Benefit From Sedation Dentistry


Sedation dentistry is not just for people with severe phobia. It is for anyone who wants the experience of dental care to feel easier, and it is an especially good fit if any of the following apply:

Fear or phobia of dental procedures

Difficulty getting fully numb with local anesthetic

A strong gag reflex

Sensitive teeth or sensitive oral nerves

A history of a difficult past dental experience

Complex or lengthy treatment ahead of you

Full-arch implant surgery or other significant procedures

Discomfort holding your mouth open for long periods

If any of these apply, ask about sedation at your consultation. Dr. Meskin will help you choose the level that fits your treatment and how you want to feel.


## Before and After Your Sedation Appointment



### Before the Appointment:


Avoid eating or drinking for 10 hours before your appointment

Take your normal medications with a sip of water, unless we instruct you otherwise

Do not smoke for 24 hours before your procedure

Wear comfortable, loose clothing

Remove jewelry, nail polish, and contact lenses

Brush your teeth as normal

Arrange for a responsible adult to drive you home


### After the Appointment:


Rest for the remainder of the day

Do not drive, operate machinery, or return to work

Avoid alcohol for at least 24 hours

Take any prescribed medications exactly as directed

Stick to soft foods and cool liquids at first

Have your companion stay with you for a few hours

Call us if anything feels wrong or unexpected


## Why Choose Hackensack Center for Sedation Dentistry


Specialist-led sedation care designed to make every visit feel calm, comfortable, and manageable.

Prosthodontist-Led Care.

Complex and full-arch cases, where sedation is often needed, are Dr. Meskin's daily work as an NYU-trained prosthodontist.

Comfort-First Environment.

A calm, judgment-free practice, designed around anxious patients, with sedation as one of several tools to make care feel manageable.

Care in Multi-Languages.

Clear communication before, during, and after sedation, in English, and Spanish

Book A Consultation


## Smile Now, Pay Later


Cherry Payment Plans

Cherry is one of the most popular healthcare financing options, built specifically for dental and medical care. You can apply in minutes with a soft credit check that does not affect your score, and qualified applicants can access 0% APR plans with no deferred interest. Payment terms range from 3 to 60 months.

Key Features:

Soft credit check, no impact to apply

0% APR for qualifying applicants, no deferred interest

Plans from 3 to 60 months

Fast online application with a quick decision

Healthcare Finance Direct

HFD focuses on making larger treatment plans manageable, with flexible structures designed to fit a range of budgets and credit situations. Our coordinators can walk you through whether HFD is the right fit for your treatment.

Options for a range of credit profiles

Flexible terms for larger cases

Guided by our treatment coordinators

Proceed Finance

Proceed specializes in financing larger and more comprehensive dental cases, such as full-arch and full-mouth treatment, with longer installment options and true 0% APR plans for those who qualify.

Built for larger, comprehensive cases

Longer-term installment options

0% APR options for qualifying applicants

CareCredit

CareCredit is a long-established healthcare credit card offering promotional no-interest periods when the balance is paid in full within the promotional window. Our coordinators will explain the terms clearly, so you know exactly how the promotional period works before you commit.

Widely accepted healthcare financing

Promotional no-interest periods when paid in full on time

Soft credit check option to apply

Request an appointment


## Frequently Asked Questions


Is sedation dentistry safe?

Yes, when it is properly planned and administered. Before any sedation, we review your health history, current medications, and allergies to confirm you are a good candidate. Your vital signs are monitored throughout the procedure. General anesthesia and IV sedation are handled by a dental anesthesiologist trained specifically for these levels of sedation.

Will I be asleep the whole time?

It depends on the level. Oral sedation keeps you relaxed but awake. IV sedation puts you in a "twilight" state where you may drift in and out but usually will not remember the procedure. General anesthesia puts you fully asleep. Dr. Meskin will help you choose the level that fits.

Will I feel any pain?

No. Sedation is used alongside local anesthetic, so the treatment area is fully numb regardless of the sedation level. Patients typically describe the experience as calm and pain-free, and often say the memory of it is hazy or absent.

How long does the sedation last?

It depends on the level. Oral sedation can leave you drowsy for several hours. IV sedation and general anesthesia typically wear off within a few hours, but you should plan to rest for the remainder of the day and avoid driving or making important decisions until the next morning.

Do I need someone to drive me home?

Yes, for any sedation level beyond very light oral sedation. You will not be permitted to drive yourself, and we ask that a responsible adult stay with you for at least a few hours after your appointment.

Can I eat before my appointment?

No, not for most sedation levels. You will need to avoid eating and drinking for 10 hours before your appointment. We will send you complete pre-appointment instructions so nothing is unclear.

How much does sedation cost?

It depends on the level and the length of your procedure. We will include sedation in your written treatment estimate up front, so there are no surprises. Financing options are available if cost is a concern.

Is sedation covered by insurance?

Sometimes, particularly when sedation is medically necessary for a specific procedure. Our team will verify your insurance benefits before treatment and let you know what may be covered.

# Cost of Dental Implants


Cost should never stand between you and the care you need. We work with every financing option available to you, and our treatment coordinators will help you find a plan that fits your budget.

Dental implants are a real investment, and we believe you deserve to see what things cost before you commit. This page walks through our starting prices for the treatments patients ask about most, the factors that change the number for your specific case, and every financing option we offer to make it manageable.

What you actually pay depends on your case, and you leave your consultation with a written estimate in your hand, not a mystery.

## What Affect the cost


The starting prices above are honest starting points, not the final number for every patient. Your specific quote depends on a handful of things, all of which are explained clearly at your consultation and included in your written estimate. Nothing is added later.

How Much Bone You Have

Implants need bone to fuse to. If the bone under a missing tooth has shrunk over the years, a bone graft may be needed before or during placement. Grafts can range from a small socket preservation done at extraction (minor cost) to a larger sinus lift or ridge augmentation (larger cost, longer timeline). Your 3D scan tells us exactly what your site needs.

Whether Extractions Are Needed

If failing teeth still need to come out, those extractions are added to your plan. For a single implant, this might mean one tooth. For a full-arch case, it can mean removing many teeth in the same appointment, which is included in most All-on-X bundles but may vary depending on how difficult the extractions are.

Sinus Lift for Upper Back Teeth

Implants in the upper back part of the mouth sometimes need extra bone underneath the sinus to hold securely. A sinus lift is a common, focused procedure, but it adds cost and healing time. Your 3D scan tells us whether yours needs one.

Number of Implants

More implants mean higher cost. A single tooth needs one. A bridge needs two. A full arch usually needs four to six, and back-of-mouth or longer-span cases sometimes need an extra implant for support. Dr. Meskin recommends the fewest that will give you a strong, lasting result.

Sedation

Placement is comfortable under local anesthetic for most patients. If you would prefer oral or IV sedation for anxiety or for a longer case, those are available and priced as an add-on.

Gum or Bite Treatment Before Implants

If active gum disease is present, it has to be treated before implants go in. Same for a bite that puts too much force on the wrong spots. This work is done first and priced separately, because your implants only last if the foundation is healthy.
